Changes made: P1: severity fixed at D1 before any run and thresholds pre-registered before D0; D0 cells raised to 8 seeds (2,800 paired) so the -5 equivalence bound sits outside the ~+/-5 contrast CI; D2 is now an unconditional, separately reported severity arm (3 seeds) that cannot rescue P1, and D3-D5 run at D1 regardless of P1. P3: pruning threshold pre-registered (25th percentile of bank scores at each checkpoint); per-item post-drift retrieval counts logged; retention split into updated-retained (>= 10 retrievals) vs frozen-retained; the prediction is pinned to the updated-retained fraction and the frozen channel is reported separately; the within-D4 LOO-anchored contrast and endogenous composition are named as what D3 cannot produce. P4: confidence gain is now computed on held-out trajectories generated without the item (pre-drift k=0 successes; post-drift k=0 and stale-removed successes), and the item-induced version is kept only as an ablation to quantify its inflation. P5: estimand redefined as the removal interaction (pairwise minus both single removals) in the mixed composition, all four cells at 8 seeds (2,800 paired), MDE ~7 net stated, prediction >= 8 net with falsifier = CI upper bound below 8 and a declared inconclusive zone; this also removes the P1-P5 shared term (P5 no longer reads off the single stale REMOVE). P2 (headline, open) unchanged in claim; the post-drift stream oversamples clean-type games to 50% and the stale class is capped at 60 items so every stale item has >= 20 post-drift retrievals per composition, making the lag measurable. Budget: dropped the position ablation and a separate REPLACE cell (fresh-only k=3 is the token-matched REPLACE of the stale item), probes cut to 3 checkpoints, closed loop to 1,000 games, no-drift control to 750; total 42,820 episodes, ~36 hours on two replicas, both GPUs busy, arithmetic stated cell by cell. Sharpness kept: the 3x lag ratio, the >= 30% vs <= 5% retention split and the >= 50% confidence-gain persistence thresholds are unchanged, and the interaction prediction is a sharper mechanism (masking of harm by co-retrieved fresh items) than the previous single-vs-pairwise disagreement.

Name: surrogate_endpoints_for_item_credit
Title: Cheaper Per-Item Credit from Process Endpoints: Variance Reduction and Class-Specific Bias of Surrogate Outcomes for Leave-One-Out Memory Value
Short Hypothesis: Per-item leave-one-out value measured on the binary success flag wastes most of each re-run; process endpoints logged in the same re-runs (goal-condition progress, steps-to-success, first-divergence step) give per-item estimates with at least three times lower noise and hence at least three times fewer re-runs for the same rank reliability, but the step-based endpoints are biased for an identifiable item class (location-stale items lengthen the path without changing success, which an equivalence test on success can show) while goal-condition progress is not, a redundant duplicate changes nothing under any endpoint, a surrogate index calibrated on natural runs with every manufactured class held out removes most of the step-endpoint bias, and zero-re-run offline surrogates (teacher-forced log-probability change, DIG-style confidence gain) do not track counterfactual value.
Related Work: DIG (arXiv:2509.12765) scores a document by generation-confidence change one document at a time, never checked against counterfactual removal (G22); MERIT (arXiv:2606.00547) and SLATE (arXiv:2602.23440) use PRM or LLM-judge step rewards as proxies whose agreement with counterfactual item value is untested; AttriMem (arXiv:2607.21106) derives local rewards from token attribution with unreported noise. Progress rewards (ProgRM arXiv:2505.18121; Progress Advantage arXiv:2606.26080) and EarlyEval (arXiv:2609.02783, halting evaluation runs early by predicting outcomes from intermediate behaviour) use process signals to cut cost but for policy training or aggregate evaluation, not per-item counterfactuals, and without class-bias tests. Surrogate-outcome methodology in trials (arXiv:2412.14129) and control variates (arXiv:2109.08944) supply the bias-variance framing; CUE-R (arXiv:2604.05467) and Shapley source attribution (arXiv:2507.04480) measure per-item effects on the answer only. Archived memory_item_value_reliability lacked an intervention arm; this idea keeps success-LOO as the anchor and asks what each re-run can additionally measure.
Abstract: Ground-truth per-item value in a memory-augmented agent is a leave-one-out re-run scored by a 0/1 success flag, so each re-run yields one bit and per-item ranks need tens of retrievals to stabilise. We ask whether the same re-runs, scored by process endpoints - fraction of PDDL goal conditions satisfied at episode end, steps-to-success, the step at which the trajectory first diverges from the intact-set run, and invalid-action counts - deliver per-item estimates that are cheaper to stabilise, and where they are biased. On the ALFWorld expert bank with Qwen3-32B at k=3 we run leave-one-out re-runs on a natural core of 500 train-stream games x 2 seeds and on manufactured item classes forced into position 3 on task-type-matched games: location-stale (a correct procedure whose object location was true in its source game but is wrong here; 30 items, 1,250 forced retrievals so the success effect is known to +/-2.5 net), planted wrong-procedure (30 items, 600 retrievals), and redundant duplicate (a paraphrase of a location-fresh item placed at position 1; 300 retrievals), plus 30 named item pairs (15 redundant, 15 cross-type controls) for pairwise removal with 20 paired episodes each. For every endpoint we estimate the retrievals needed for rank reliability 0.7 (read directly on the forced panel, extrapolated on natural items), the raw rank correlation with success-LOO on natural items, and the class-wise bias in net points against an equivalence-tested success effect; a logistic surrogate index of success on the process endpoints is cross-fitted on natural runs with every manufactured class held out and tested for residual class bias; offline surrogates that need no re-runs are scored the same way. Static-prompt arms (a type-level procedure sentence and an instance-location sentence) are paired on the same forced episodes, and a second reader re-measures the stale class at the same precision. About 18,000 episodes (16 h on two A100s) yield a re-run savings factor per endpoint, a bias map by item class, and a calibrated estimator whose cost and bias are both stated.
Experiments: Pilot (500 episodes, run first): seed component on 125 games x 2 seeds x (base + remove-3); item-following rate for stale items (fraction of episodes whose first receptacle visited is the one named by the position-3 item); planted-wrong harm check (items whose success-LOO harm is under 20 net in a 100-episode cell are replaced by stronger wrong procedures before E1); goal-condition fraction validated against the success flag (fraction 1 iff success); per-episode SD of every endpoint, used to confirm the cell sizes below. E0 (no environment steps; one GPU while the pilot and E1 run on the other): offline surrogates for every item in the k=3 logs - teacher-forced log-probability of the expert action sequence under the prompt with vs without the item, and DIG-style confidence gain on the base trajectory - about 3 forward passes per episode on 2,000 episodes. E1-N natural core: 500 train-stream games x 2 seeds x natural top-3, base + 3 single removals = 4,000 episodes; every run logs success, goal-condition fraction per step (satisfied PDDL goal predicates), steps to success or max, first-divergence step relative to the intact-set run under the same seed, and invalid or repeated action counts. E1-F forced classes (position 3 forced on task-type-matched games; runs = base + remove-3): location-stale, 30 items on 1,250 distinct (game, seed) = 2,500 episodes (about 42 retrievals per item; +/-2.5 net on success at per-episode delta SD 0.45); planted wrong-procedure, 30 items on 600 = 1,200 episodes (+/-3.6 net); composition is a within-cell factor: 250 stale and 120 planted retrievals use a stripped set whose position 2 is a token-matched cross-type item, the rest keep the natural top-2; remove-1 and remove-2 on 300 forced episodes = 600 episodes give natural-item values under forced composition. E1-F total 4,300. E2 named pairs: 15 location-fresh items (the stale items' siblings with the correct receptacle for the game) forced into position 1 on 20 (game, seed) each, under two compositions - A: [fresh, natural-2, paraphrase of fresh] (redundant pairs; remove-3 alone is the duplicate class, 300 retrievals) and B: [fresh, natural-2, token-matched cross-type item] (control pairs; remove-3 alone is the cross-type class, 300 retrievals) - with runs base, remove-1, remove-3, remove-1+3: 15 x 20 x 4 x 2 = 2,400 episodes; every named pair has 20 paired episodes. E4 static-prompt arms, paired on the same (game, seed, item) episodes as E1-F: type-level procedure sentence (Measurement C) on 400 stale retrievals (800 episodes), 600 planted retrievals (1,200) and 100 natural games x 2 seeds x 4 runs (800, natural-item value net of static); instance-location sentence (a static line naming the target object's correct receptacle for this game) on the same 400 stale retrievals (800); E4 total 3,600. E5 consumer swap under the second local backbone (serving verified beforehand): 150 natural games x 2 seeds x 4 = 1,200 (reader-2 natural-item SD units and reader-2 index fit) + 1,000 stale retrievals x 2 = 2,000 (+/-2.8 net); E5 total 3,200. E7 surrogate index: logistic regression of success on the process endpoints fitted on E1-N natural episodes of one game half, applied to the other half's LOO re-runs and to every forced-class re-run, and vice versa; the manufactured classes never enter the fit; no extra episodes. Analyses per endpoint Z: delta_Z per (item, game, seed); crossed variance components (item, game, seed); split-half reliability over games at each n by retrieval subsampling, read directly on the 30-item stale panel up to n = 42 and by Spearman-Brown on natural items; n_Z(0.7) and savings = n_success(0.7)/n_Z(0.7) with a paired bootstrap over games and items; raw Spearman between item means under Z and under success on natural items with >= 20 retrievals; class means under Z in SD of natural-item means against class means under success in net points; index bias = index-predicted net minus success-LOO net on the same episodes. Total 500 + 4,000 + 4,300 + 2,400 + 3,600 + 3,200 = 18,000 episodes; at about 1,150 episodes/h with both replicas busy (the rate behind the original 8,000-in-7-h sizing) this is about 16 h; pre-registration after the pilot.
Baselines and Ablations: Success-LOO as the reference estimator; each raw process endpoint; the cross-fitted surrogate index with the manufactured classes held out, fitted with and without the first-divergence feature to see which endpoint carries the bias; offline surrogates (teacher-forced expert log-probability change; DIG-style confidence gain); an early-halt variant computed from the per-step progress logs (progress at 50% of the step limit) as the cheapest process surrogate; manufactured classes (location-stale, planted wrong-procedure, redundant duplicate) plus location-fresh siblings and token-matched cross-type items against natural items; natural vs forced composition for natural items and natural top-2 vs stripped position 2 within the stale cell; single vs pairwise removal on 30 named pairs; gross vs type-level static-procedure net (Measurement C) and vs an instance-location sentence; two readers.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 Savings (headline; E1-N natural items and the E1-F stale panel, the same re-runs scored under both endpoints): goal-condition-progress LOO reaches split-half rank reliability 0.7 with at most one third of the retrievals success-LOO needs (savings >= 3x); falsified if savings < 1.5x with the paired-bootstrap 95% CI on the ratio excluding 3x. n_Z(0.7) is read directly from the observed curve on the 30 stale items (42 retrievals each on distinct games) and by Spearman-Brown on the >= 100 natural items with >= 20 retrievals, both reported. Not entailed because progress may be as bimodal as success (its top mass is pinned to success by the validation) and the ratio may fall below 1.5x. P2 Class bias (E1-F stale cell, 1,250 retrievals, +/-2.5 net): (a) success branch as a pre-registered TOST equivalence: the stale class's success-LOO lies within +/-6 net (90% CI inside the bounds); falsified if the 95% CI excludes zero and the point estimate is <= -5 net (the step endpoints would then be right, not biased). (b) steps-to-success and first-divergence assign the stale class <= -0.3 SD of natural-item means with 95% CI excluding -0.1 SD; falsified if the class lies within +/-0.1 SD - reachable because the reader follows a retrieved location hint in only a fraction of episodes (following rate logged as the manipulation check; a rate below about 30% makes the detour vanish) and because the stale receptacle may lie on the reader's default search order, in which case there is no detour. (c) goal-condition progress is unbiased for the stale class (within +/-0.1 SD); falsified if progress puts it <= -0.3 SD. (d) the duplicate class (E2 composition A, remove-3, 300 retrievals) is a negative control expected within +/-0.1 SD under every endpoint and within +/-5 net under success; any endpoint assigning it |value| > 0.3 SD is reported as a false positive of that endpoint. P3 Calibrated index (E7, classes held out of the fit): (a) raw un-disattenuated Spearman between index-LOO and success-LOO item means on the >= 100 natural items with >= 20 retrievals is >= 0.5 with 95% bootstrap CI excluding 0.3, computed only where both arms' split-half reliability is >= 0.5 (otherwise at the retrieval count where success reaches 0.5); falsified if the CI lies below 0.4; disattenuated values are reported but carry no prediction. (b) the stale-class index bias (index-predicted net minus success-LOO net on the same episodes) is within +/-4 net; falsified if the CI on the bias excludes zero and the point is <= -6 net (the index inherits the step-endpoint bias because path length carries weight in natural runs) - reachable because the classes never enter the fit. (c) the planted-wrong index bias is within +/-5 net (+/-3.6 net CI); falsified if the CI excludes zero and |point| >= 8 net. The index's n(0.7) is reported, with no separate savings prediction, since it is bounded by P1. P4 Offline surrogates (E0 vs E1-N): each of teacher-forced expert log-probability change and DIG-style confidence gain has raw Spearman < 0.25 with success-LOO item means on the same natural items, and separates planted-wrong from location-stale items with AUC < 0.7 (30 vs 30 items); falsified if raw Spearman >= 0.4 with CI excluding 0.25, or AUC >= 0.85. P5 Non-additivity (E2, 15 redundant pairs = fresh item at position 1 + its paraphrase at position 3, 15 control pairs = the same fresh item + a token-matched cross-type item, 20 paired episodes each, 4 runs): under the progress endpoint >= 60% of redundant pairs show pair-minus-sum-of-singles with 95% CI excluding zero on the sub-additive side, versus <= 20% under success on the same episodes, and <= 20% of control pairs are flagged under progress; falsified if progress flags <= 30% of redundant pairs, or flags >= 40% of control pairs (the surrogate manufactures interactions), or if the pooled success-endpoint interaction over the redundant pairs (300 paired episodes, CI about +/-10 net) has a CI including zero while progress flags them (the progress detections are then artifacts, since there is no success-relevant redundancy to detect). The redundant-pair detection ratio between endpoints inherits P1's variance ratio and is reported as such; the control false-positive rate and the pooled-success confirmation are the independent content. P6 Consumer swap (E5, reader 2: 1,000 stale retrievals, +/-2.8 net; 150 natural games for reader-2 SD units and index): the P2 pattern replicates - the stale class's step-endpoint value is <= -0.3 SD of reader-2 natural-item means with CI excluding -0.1 SD, and its success-LOO passes the same +/-6 net TOST; falsified if reader 2's step endpoint puts the stale class within +/-0.1 SD, or if the success CI excludes zero with point <= -5 net. P7 Static net (E4, paired on the same forced (game, seed, item) episodes as E1-F): (a) type-level procedure sentence: the planted-wrong class's success-LOO harm (pilot-verified >= 20 net) shrinks by >= 50% as a paired difference-in-differences (point >= 50%, CI excluding 25%; CI about +/-20 percentage points at 600 paired retrievals); falsified if the point shrink is <= 20% with CI excluding 50%. (b) type-level sentence: the stale class keeps its step-endpoint penalty (<= -0.3 SD at 400 paired retrievals); falsified if it moves within +/-0.1 SD - reachable if the sentence lowers the item-following rate (logged in both arms) so that the reader stops using the retrieved location. (c) instance-location sentence: the stale class's extra-steps penalty (paired steps-to-success difference against remove-3, in raw steps) shrinks by >= 50% (point, CI excluding 20%; +/-1 step at 400 paired retrievals if per-episode step SD <= 10, pilot-checked); falsified if it shrinks by <= 20% with CI excluding 50% (the reader trusts the retrieved episode over the static correct location).
Measurement and Noise Control: Every endpoint is computed on the same re-runs, so comparisons between endpoints are within-episode paired and their reliability differences are bootstrapped over games and items with the pairing preserved; reliability is split-half over games (seed replicates of a game are never split across halves) and the crossed variance components separate item, game and seed. Cell sizes at per-episode success-delta SD 0.45 (pilot-confirmed): stale 1,250 forced retrievals (+/-2.5 net), planted 600 (+/-3.6 net), duplicate and cross-type 300 each (+/-5 net), reader-2 stale 1,000 (+/-2.8 net); the equivalence claims are pre-registered TOST tests with bounds +/-6 net, outside every stale CI, so 'no success effect' and 'the surrogate is right' are separable. Step-endpoint class values are in SD of natural-item means (>= 100 items with >= 20 retrievals; +/-0.1 SD at 400 retrievals if the per-episode step SD in those units is <= 1, pilot-checked, cells enlarged from the remaining budget otherwise); the instance-location contrast is in raw steps (+/-1 step at 400 paired retrievals if per-episode step SD <= 10). Rank agreement is the raw Spearman with a bootstrap CI over items; disattenuated values are reported but carry no prediction, and any comparison at a retrieval count where either arm's split-half reliability is below 0.5 is moved to the count where it reaches 0.5. The surrogate index is cross-fitted across game halves on natural episodes only; the manufactured classes never enter the fit. All static-prompt arms are paired on the same (game, seed, item) episodes and analysed as paired differences. Item-following rate (first receptacle visited equals the receptacle named by the position-3 item) is logged in every forced episode and reported per arm as the manipulation check. Planted-wrong items with pilot harm under 20 net are replaced before E1. Goal-condition fraction is validated against the success flag (1 iff success) before use. Sampling temperature fixed and reported; seed component measured first; all thresholds pre-registered after the pilot; both replicas busy (E0 and the pilot overlap, then E1-N and E1-F split across the two replicas, E4 and E5 overlapped with E2) with throughput logged per cell.
Preprint Collision Check: All queries answered by the literature command (Semantic Scholar + HF Papers, both ok); WebSearch not used. (1) home: 'surrogate index variance reduction control variates online experiments CUPED long-term outcome': no CUPED or surrogate-index paper returned (Deng et al. 2013 and Athey et al. 2019 are cited from memory); nearest returned items are a model-free surrogate for survival endpoints arXiv:2412.14129 and control-variate papers arXiv:2109.08944, arXiv:2305.00402, arXiv:2212.00517; nothing applies surrogate endpoints to per-item counterfactual valuation. (2) mechanism, --recent: 'progress-based surrogate outcome instead of binary success variance reduction LLM agent evaluation fewer rollouts': EarlyEval arXiv:2609.02783 (2026-09-02; early outcome prediction to halt evaluation runs; aggregate accuracy, not per-item counterfactuals, no class bias), VIGOR arXiv:2607.22002 (rollout allocation by reward variance), Progress Advantage arXiv:2606.26080 and ProgRM arXiv:2505.18121 (progress rewards for training), SEAGym arXiv:2606.17546; none estimates per-item value. (3) closest named method: DIG (digest card arXiv:2509.12765) and the RAG Shapley query 'Shapley attribution retrieved documents RAG LLM calls approximation redundancy evidence utility intervention', which returned only arXiv:2507.04480 (answer-level attribution, single-shot). (4) --recent 'per-item value of retrieved memory leave-one-out noise seeds sample size LLM agent' returned nothing on surrogate endpoints (Echo Gap arXiv:2608.00017, MEMPROBE arXiv:2606.24595 unrelated). No preprint reports a re-run savings factor or a class-bias map for process-endpoint estimates of memory item value.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Goal-condition fraction may require a custom PDDL predicate check in the ALFWorld text engine (implementation risk; fallback is subgoal completion inferred from the expert plan's object states). First-divergence step under sampled decoding is noisy even with a fixed seed because the prompts differ; its reliability curve is reported like any other endpoint and it may simply lose to progress. Items that induce short failing episodes (early done) can game step-based endpoints; the first-divergence and progress endpoints and the index are expected to expose this, and it is reported if not. If the reader follows retrieved location hints rarely, P2(b), P6 and P7(b, c) fail together; the following rate is a logged manipulation check, not an excuse. The stale-class equivalence at +/-6 net cannot rule out a 3-4 net success effect; such an outcome is reported as 'bias not established'. If location-fresh items carry under 10 net joint value the pooled-success confirmation in P5 is underpowered and is reported as such. The index's bias correction assumes surrogacy transfers from natural runs to the held-out classes, which P3(b) may reject. The second-backbone serving must be verified before E5. Results depend on ALFWorld's procedural structure with clear subgoals and may not transfer to tasks without decomposable progress; location-stale items are an ALFWorld analogue of staleness, not temporal drift. REPLACE ground truth and a store-size arm were cut to fund the class cells; total compute is about 16 h on two A100s.
Addresses gap: G24 (sample and compute cost of per-item estimates: the re-run savings factor is the estimand) and G22 (offline proxy signals such as DIG-style confidence gain are checked against counterfactual removal of the same item).
Not a restatement of: Nearest brief bullet: 'Cost: a leave-one-out re-run of one episode costs one episode; Shapley over a k=3 set costs 7 re-runs per episode' - the brief prices ground truth per re-run on the binary outcome; this idea claims the same re-run carries a lower-variance endpoint whose class-specific bias can be measured and corrected, and measures both the savings and the bias. Nearest digest card: arXiv:2509.12765 (DIG scores one document by confidence change, never checked against counterfactual removal, interactions and transfer untested) - this idea checks DIG-style and teacher-forced offline surrogates plus three process endpoints against success-LOO in a multi-step agent, under two compositions, on 30 named item pairs, under two readers and two static-prompt arms, with class-level bias as a reported quantity. Nearest archived idea: memory_item_value_reliability had no intervention arm; here success-LOO remains the anchor and the question is what else each intervention re-run measures.
Changes made: P2: stale cell enlarged from about 400 to 1,250 forced retrievals (CI +/-2.5 net) and the success branch restated as a pre-registered TOST equivalence with bounds +/-6 net, falsifier = CI excludes zero with point <= -5 net; the step branch names its reachable falsifiers (item-following rate and default search order, logged as a manipulation check) and a progress no-bias clause is added; the duplicate control is kept as a reported false-positive check. P3: raw un-disattenuated Spearman with bootstrap CI and a 0.5 reliability floor replaces the disattenuated 0.8; the three classes are held out of the index fit so class bias is an out-of-class test with thresholds separated by the stale CI; the savings clause (a copy of P1) was dropped. P4: moved to raw Spearman with thresholds scaled to the reliability ceiling so the divisor shared with P3 is gone. P5: two position-pairs replaced by 30 named pairs (15 redundant fresh+paraphrase, 15 cross-type controls) x 20 paired episodes x 4 runs; estimand = detection rate, with the control false-positive rate and a pooled success-endpoint confirmation as content independent of P1. P6: store-size clause and E6 cut; reader-2 stale cell sized to 1,000 retrievals (+/-2.8 net) with the same TOST and step thresholds as P2. P7: static arms now paired on the same forced episodes at 400-600 retrievals, planted harm pre-verified >= 20 net so 50% vs 20% shrink are separable at +/-20 pp, an instance-location sentence arm added so the stale branch can fail, and the type-level branch names its reachable falsifier (following-rate collapse). P1 (headline) unchanged in claim; n_Z(0.7) is now read directly on the 30-item stale panel (42 retrievals each) instead of extrapolated. Cuts to fund the cells: E3 REPLACE arm and E6 store-size arm removed; the natural core reduced from 1,000 to 500 games x 2 seeds; total 18,000 episodes, about 16 h on two A100s. The central claims (>= 3x savings, step-endpoint bias on stale items with unbiased progress, index removes the bias, offline surrogates fail) are unchanged in magnitude; no threshold was softened.

Name: item_value_consumer_decomposition
Title: Whose Value Is It? Decomposing Retrieved-Item Counterfactual Value into a Consumer-Invariant Procedure Part and a Consumer-Specific Residual
Short Hypothesis: The leave-one-out value of a retrieved experience item is the sum of a type-level part that the best static type-conditioned arm (static3: three fixed expert exemplars, +12.4 net over k=0 under Qwen3-32B) already carries and that transfers across readers, and an item-specific residual (the per-item composition of the measured +17.2 net that k=3 retrieval adds over static3) that is reliable within a reader but does not transfer. On identical retrieved sets: the disattenuated cross-reader rank agreement of item residuals is below 0.5 while within-reader split-half reliability is at least 0.5; the residual concentrates in item classes that invite verbatim copying (long-detour self-written trajectories) and costs a weaker reader more than a stronger one; value-guided item selection estimated under one reader is worthless under another; and the residual is a property of the backbone rather than of its current policy, so it survives self-distillation of the same reader but not a capability-matched reader of another family.
Related Work: Per-item value is measured by intervention only under one generator: CUE-R REMOVE/REPLACE (2604.05467), document Shapley (2507.04480), DIG confidence gain (2509.12765, which explicitly does not examine transfer across generators). Agent memory systems claim model-agnosticism at the system level: ExpGraph/ExpSuite (2605.30712) swaps frozen executors and ablates modules, ReMe (2512.10696) reports that a smaller model with memory beats a larger one without, and CHIME (2609.02074) evolves separate planning and execution banks with attribute-before-memorize; none asks whether the utility of an individual experience learned under executor A is its utility under executor B. In the home literature, training-data value is known to be model-dependent (Data Shapley 1904.02868; DataInf 2310.00902) and proxy-model transfer of data-curation decisions is unreliable (2512.24503; DataDecide 2504.11393 finds it works only for likelihood-type proxies); this idea imports that question to in-context retrieved items with an intervention ground truth and a decomposition. The program's own memory_item_value_reliability (6.12) asserted that item value is not an item property but had no intervention arm.
Abstract: Every self-evolving memory system scores its items, and several claim the scores are model-agnostic, yet no per-item score has been re-measured under a second consumer. We ask whether the counterfactual value of a retrieved ALFWorld experience item belongs to the item or to the reader that consumes it. Holding the retrieved sets fixed (the logged rank-ordered ids from the k-sweep), we measure leave-one-out (REMOVE) and token-matched REPLACE effects of the same items under Qwen3-32B (reader A), Qwen3-8B (reader B: same family, weaker), gemma-3-27b-it (reader D: other family, capability-matched) and a self-distilled LoRA variant of Qwen3-32B (reader C: same backbone, shifted policy, the drift case of G16). Item value is decomposed against Measurement C's best static arm (static3, +12.4 over k=0; k=3 adds +17.2 over it under A): the type-level part is what static3 carries, the residual is the item's REMOVE effect with static3 present. Item classes are manufactured as with-arms at position 1 of the same natural set, so class comparisons are direct paired contrasts on the same (game, seed): planted wrong-procedure, cross-type token-matched placebo, short and long-detour self-written. Transfer is tested at matched noise by the disattenuated cross-reader Spearman of item residuals with a bootstrap CI on the ratio itself, and its operational consequence by cross-fitted, shrinkage-corrected value-guided top-3 selection estimated under one reader and deployed under another, paired game by game at 2,740 episodes per arm. Readers C and D separate a policy shift from a backbone swap at matched capability. The contribution is a statement of what a per-item score means when the reader changes: which component transfers, which does not, in which classes the non-transferable part lives, whether it is a backbone or a policy property, and at what re-run cost the residual can be estimated to a stable rank.
Experiments: Setting: ALFWorld, expert bank, bank-target partition as in the starting position; 274 valid games (seen+unseen); a cell is 274 games x S seeds of paired episodes with S chosen per arm (S=4: 1,096, +/-5.7; S=6: 1,644, +/-4.6; S=10: 2,740, +/-3.6, scaled from the measured +/-8 at 548). Retrieved sets are frozen to the logged rank-ordered ids (retrieval is by task-text similarity and does not depend on the reader), so the reader is the only manipulated variable. Static arm = static3 (Measurement C's best static arm: 3 fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, ~430 tokens, cached). Readers: A Qwen3-32B (GPU0), B Qwen3-8B (same family, weaker; GPU1), D gemma-3-27b-it (other family, capability-matched to A), C Qwen3-32B plus the program's self-distilled LoRA (same backbone, shifted policy). E0 (reported arm, not a gate): reader B k-sweep k in {0,1,3,7} on the logged sets at S=4 (k=3 at S=10 because it doubles as the similarity top-3 arm of E4); B's k3-k0 and k3-static3 are reported whatever they are, and every later arm runs under B regardless, so a reader that ignores item content is an outcome P1 records, not a screen. E1 ground truth per reader (A, B): REMOVE position 1 (S=6; also the shared without-arm of E3), REMOVE 2/3 (S=4), token-matched cross-type REPLACE at position 1 (S=4), k=1 vs k=0 as the second set composition (S=4), pairwise removal of all three pairs on 1 seed (822) for additivity, item-order shuffle on 1 seed (274); logged k-sweep and static3 arms under A are reused and topped up to the required S. E2 decomposition per reader (A, B): static3 (S=4), static3+k3 (S=6), static3+REMOVE 1/2/3 (S=6; 4,932 residual contrasts per reader); residual_i = success(static3+k3) minus success(static3+k3 without i) on the same (game, seed); procedural part of an item's type = static3 minus k0; per-item analysis on items with >= 8 residual contrasts (expected 150-250 items, each retrieved for >= 2 games and so with >= 12 contrasts at S=6). E3 manufactured classes, all as with-arms at position 1 of the natural k=3 set on the same (game, seed), so class comparisons are direct paired with-vs-with contrasts and never differences of two cells: C1 = natural same-type expert (the k=3 arm), C2 planted wrong-procedure (same-type expert trajectory with the procedure receptacle swapped, e.g. clean with microwave), C3 cross-type token-matched placebo, both S=6; C4 self-written same-type short (<= median length) and C5 self-written same-type long-detour (>= 2x median navigation steps), both S=10; class nets against the shared REMOVE-1 without-arm are secondary. E4 cross-fitted deployment: item values (residual + procedural, James-Stein-shrunk toward the class mean with weights from contrast count, pre-registered) averaged over an item's fold-1 retrievals pick the top 3 of the top-10 similarity candidates for fold-2 games, cross-fitted in both directions so every game is deployed once per seed; arms at S=10 (2,740): under B: A-values, B-values, random-3 (similarity top-3 = the natural k=3 arm); under A: A-values, B-values (similarity top-3 = the natural k=3 arm); all arms of a reader are paired game by game. E5 readers C and D: k0, k1, k3, static3, static3+k3, static3+REMOVE 1/2/3 at S=4 (8,768 each), giving their residuals on the same items, split-half rho_CC and rho_DD, the k=1 second composition, and C's k=0 manipulation check. Budget (episodes): A 30,688 (E1 9,316 including top-ups of k0/k1/k3/static3; E2 7,124; E3 8,768; E4 5,480); B 36,716 (E0/E1 12,056; E2 7,672; E3 8,768; E4 8,220); C 8,768; D 8,768; total 84,940. Wall: A at ~10 episodes/min on one replica = 51 h on GPU0; B at ~25/min = 24.5 h, then D and C at ~10/min = 14.6 h each on GPU1 (53.7 h); ~2.2 days with both GPUs busy, ~2.5 days with restarts; the earlier plan's cross-family 8B reader and the E1 arms of C/D were cut to pay for the larger E3/E4 cells. One vLLM replica per GPU, workers raised until each replica's running queue is >= 8. Order: E0-E2 on both GPUs first, then E3, E4 (needs E2's values), then E5. Thresholds pre-registered before E1.
Baselines and Ablations: k=0 and static3 arms per reader (procedural credit subtracted before any item claim); token-matched REPLACE vs REMOVE (content vs length); k=1 vs k=3 REMOVE (set composition) and pairwise vs single removal (additivity) under A and B, k=1 vs k=3 under C and D; item-order shuffle control on 1 seed; reader design as a factorial on family, capability and policy: A vs B (same family, weaker), A vs D (other family, capability-matched), A vs C (same backbone, self-distilled policy, valid only if C's k=0 success differs from A's by >= 5 net), so family distance, capability and policy shift are separated; the A split-half correlation is the ceiling every cross-reader correlation is disattenuated against; for E4, in-reader cross-fitted selection is the upper bound, random-3 from the top-10 candidates the floor, similarity top-3 (the natural k=3 arm) the reference, and unshrunk ranking is the ablation of the pre-registered James-Stein shrinkage; subsampling curves (rank correlation between estimates from n and from all contrasts) report the re-runs needed for a stable per-item rank against the LOO baseline cost of one re-run per item per episode.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (class-level transfer, positive control): under both A and B the with-arms at position 1 of the same k=3 set order as C2 planted wrong-procedure < C3 placebo < C1 natural same-type expert, and the direct paired C1 minus C2 contrast is >= +10 net in each reader. C1 and C2 are with-arms on the same (game, seed), so C1-C2 is one paired contrast at 1,644 episodes (+/-4.6), not a difference of two cells, and the +/-5 equivalence band exceeds its CI. Falsified under B if C1-C2 is <= +5 (its CI then excludes +10) or if C2 >= C3 (a planted wrong procedure costs nothing more than a placebo); produced by the E3 arms under B, which run whatever the E0 k-sweep shows, so a weaker reader that ignores item content is a recorded outcome, not a screened one; not entailed, since E0 no longer selects B for consuming items. P2 (residual non-transfer, headline): the disattenuated cross-reader Spearman of item residuals, rho_AB / sqrt(rho_AA rho_BB), is < 0.5 while the within-reader split-half reliabilities rho_AA and rho_BB (seeds 1-3 vs 4-6) are >= 0.5; the aggregate residual under A is the measured +17.2 over static3, and the claim is about its per-item composition, not its magnitude. P5 (policy shift vs backbone swap): disattenuated rho_AC (self-distilled Qwen3-32B) is >= 0.8 and disattenuated rho_AD (gemma-3-27b-it, capability-matched, other family) is < 0.5, both against the same A split-half ceiling and with item-bootstrap CIs (about +/-0.25); the C half is valid only if C's k=0 success differs from A's by >= 5 net (the manipulation check that the policy moved), otherwise it is reported as untested. Falsified if rho_AC is < 0.5 with rho_CC >= 0.5 (a policy shift alone re-ranks the items: the residual is a policy property, the G16 drift outcome), or if rho_AD is >= 0.8 (a capability-matched reader of another family agrees with A, so non-transfer to B was capability, not reader identity); produced by the E5 residual arms under C and D. Not entailed by the shared backbone: reader C is trained on A's own successes with these items in context, so it may have internalized their content, which would collapse (rho_CC < 0.5) or re-rank (rho_AC < 0.5) its residuals, and the prediction is an absolute level against the A ceiling rather than a comparison with rho_AB. P1 is the positive control required before any null in P2-P5 is reported.
Measurement and Noise Control: Every value is a paired contrast on the same (game, seed, retrieved set): net = 100 x (success with minus success without), CIs by game-level bootstrap (2,000 resamples) with seed as a blocking factor; cells sized from the measured floor (+/-8 at 548 paired episodes: +/-5.7 at 1,096, +/-4.6 at 1,644, +/-3.6 at 2,740). Class comparisons (P1, P3) and deployment comparisons (P4) are direct paired contrasts between two with-arms on the same (game, seed), whose CI is taken to be no wider than the with/without floor; this is re-estimated from the first two seeds of E3 and cells are topped up if wider, so no prediction rests on a difference of two independent cells and no two predictions share a without-baseline. Item-level quantities are reported as distributions, never as individual effects; per-item residuals use items with >= 8 contrasts (expected 150-250 items, >= 12 contrasts each at S=6); transfer is a comparison of correlations computed from the same contrasts per item, disattenuated by split-half reliabilities on the same items, and the CI of the disattenuated ratio itself (not of a raw Spearman) is estimated by item bootstrap with the split-half re-drawn, expected about +/-0.25 at 200 items. Binding reference: k3 minus static3 = +17.2 [+11.9, +22.4] under A (Measurement C); all residuals are net of static3, no prediction assumes that aggregate is null under any reader, and B's, C's and D's k3 minus static3 are reported arms. Estimator cost is an estimand: subsampling curves give the re-runs per item for a rank correlation of 0.8 with the full estimate, and LLM-call cost is reported per reader. Seeds and vLLM versions pinned; each arm logged as resumable JSONL under nohup with pid files; one replica per GPU, workers raised until each replica's running queue is >= 8 and utilization >= 50%; throughput reported per replica.

Name: slot_vs_item_credit_permutation
Title: Slot or Item: Separating Position Credit from Content Credit in Retrieved Sets by Permutation and Leave-One-Out
Short Hypothesis: The per-position marginal value read off nested-k retrieval logs (k=1 within k=3 within k=7) confounds an item's content with its slot. Permuting the same k=3 set on the same (game, seed) separates the two. On sets whose three items share the game's task type, reversing the order is equivalent to no change within 5 net; on mixed sets, moving the single same-type item from slot 1 to slot 3 costs at least 8 net, and a planted conflicting item harms at least 8 net more in slot 1 than in slot 3. The premium is a slot-1 step, not a gradient and not lost-in-the-middle: slot 2 sits close to slot 3 on both the help side and the harm side, which is the signature of early adoption of the first item read. The nested-k rank-1 credit therefore contains a slot component of at least 8 net on mixed sets that must be removed before it is used as item credit, and the premium survives at k=7.
Related Work: Lost-in-the-middle position effects are established for long-context QA and revisited for RAG, where arxiv:2505.15561 (EMNLP 2025) finds distracting top-ranked passages matter more than position; primacy in MCQA option order (arxiv:2507.13949); demonstration-order sensitivity of in-context learning is the home literature (order permutations change few-shot accuracy; permutation-invariance violations as a source of order-induced errors, arxiv:2509.11208; PICASO arxiv:2502.17605). None permutes retrieved experience in a multi-step agent or measures the slot component of an item's leave-one-out credit. The compliance trap (arxiv:2607.10608) locates harm at the first exposed decision point but does not manipulate slot. DIG (arxiv:2509.12765) scores one document at a time and ignores order; CUE-R (arxiv:2604.05467) does not permute. The brief's nested-k per-position counterfactual is the object corrected here. Archived: action_prior_imprinting (5.27) and memory_budget_confound (5.63) concern priors and volume, not slot; retrieved_set_disagreement_gate (4.65) had no item-level ground truth.
Abstract: Retrieval logs that nest k=1 within k=3 within k=7 on the same games seem to give a per-position counterfactual for free, and every ranked memory system implicitly treats the rank-1 slot as the most valuable. But the item at rank 1 is both the most similar item and the first item the reader sees, so its measured credit mixes content with slot. We separate them by permutation on ALFWorld with a Qwen3-32B reader, on pools whose size is fixed before any rollout from retrieval alone and set by the minimum detectable effect rather than by what the logs happen to contain. On 200 ALL-SAME games the natural k=3 set is run in original and reversed order and tested for equivalence; on 200 MIXED games the single same-type item is shown in slot 1, 2 or 3 with the two cross-type items in fixed order, which by construction measures the slot component of that item's leave-one-out credit as an absolute net difference; on 160 procedure-type games a token-matched conflicting item is planted in slot 1, 2 or 3, giving the sign and shape of the slot effect for harm and separating a slot-1 step (early adoption) from lost-in-the-middle and recency; a k=7 arm moves the same-type item from slot 1 to slot 7. No-op repeats give the noise floor as an estimand, and every pre-registered threshold pair is separated by twice the design half-width. We predict that order is inert among consistent items, that the same-type item is worth at least 8 net more in slot 1 than in slot 3 and at least 7 net more than in slot 2, that a planted conflict harms at least 8 net more in slot 1 than in slot 3 with the drop concentrated between slots 1 and 2, and that the premium survives at k=7. The result tells the program whether its free per-position estimate is usable as item credit, by how many net points it overstates rank-1 credit on mixed sets, and how retrieval rank should be read when items are scored.
Experiments: (0) Pools, fixed before any rollout from retrieval alone (no reader calls): every natural k=3 set of the 274 validation games and of the bank-disjoint train slice is classified as ALL-SAME (three items of the game's task type), MIXED (exactly one same-type item; its natural rank 1, 2 or 3 recorded) or ALL-CROSS (dropped). Pool sizes are set from the minimum detectable effect: ALL-SAME pool = 200 games; MIXED pool = 200 games (validation first, then train slice; if natural MIXED sets run short, a MIXED set is composed from the game's own natural top-7 list as its top same-type item plus its two top cross-type items, flagged as composed and reported separately); PROC pool = 160 procedure-type games (clean, heat, cool) whose natural k=3 set is ALL-SAME, overlapping the ALL-SAME pool where possible. Reader Qwen3-32B on two vLLM replicas, expert bank, prompt template and item numbering held fixed, token counts logged. (1) ALL-SAME order arm (P1): O = (a,b,c) and R = (c,b,a), 200 games x 6 seeds x 2 = 2,400 episodes; no-op repeat O' on 100 games x 4 seeds = 400 episodes. (2) MIXED forced-slot arm (P2 headline, P6): the same-type item in slot 1 (S1), slot 2 (S2) or slot 3 (S3) with the two cross-type items in their natural relative order; S1 and S3 at 200 games x 8 seeds = 3,200 episodes, S2 at 200 games x 6 seeds = 1,200 episodes; no-op repeat S1' on 100 games x 4 seeds = 400 episodes. Because the residual pair is identical across S1, S2 and S3, f(S1) - f(S3) is exactly the difference between the same-type item's leave-one-out credit measured in slot 1 and in slot 3 (the LOO cell f(residual pair) cancels), i.e. the slot component of the natural-order LOO credit; no separate LOO cell is needed and none is run. (3) Planted-conflict slot arm (P3, P4): a token-matched wrong-procedure item (CONFLICT class of the pairwise audit) replaces the natural rank-3 item and is shown in slot 1 (C1), 2 (C2) or 3 (C3) with the two natural same-type items shifted in their natural order: 160 games x 8 seeds x 3 = 3,840 episodes; the unplanted reference U is the ALL-SAME O cell for PROC games inside the ALL-SAME pool and is run at 4 seeds for the rest (at most 640, expected ~250 episodes). (4) k=7 arm (P5): for the MIXED pool, the same-type item plus the six top cross-type items of the game's natural ranked list, shown with the same-type item in slot 1 (S1@7) or slot 7 (S7@7): 200 games x 4 seeds x 2 = 1,600 episodes at ~1.5x the per-episode cost of k=3. (5) Nested-k reanalysis: the logs' k=1-vs-k=0 and k=3-vs-k=1 contrasts (the free per-position profile) are re-read against the slot components measured in (2) and (4), reported as absolute net with CIs, and the corrected profile is set beside the static3 residual of Measurement C. (6) Gates, run first: C1 vs U harm >= 10 net (PROC, 4 seeds) and S1 minus the logs' k=0 >= +10 net on validation MIXED games; the no-op repeats must give |f(O') - f(O)| and |f(S1') - f(S1)| <= 5 net, otherwise the design half-widths are recomputed from the observed flip rate and the affected pool is extended by up to 100 train-slice games at 4 seeds (capped at 1,600 episodes) before any prediction is read. Total ~13,300 episodes (~14,100 k=3-equivalents), ~12 h on two A100s at the ~1,200 episodes/h of the k-sweep; arms (1)-(3) are queued as one job across both replicas so neither GPU idles.
Baselines and Ablations: No-op repeats (O', S1') as the empirical noise floor for order effects; ALL-SAME O vs R as the consistent-content control; forced-slot S1/S2/S3 on MIXED sets as the slot manipulation with the item set and the residual order fixed; planted-conflict C1/C2/C3 against the unplanted reference U to separate a slot-1 step, a gradient, lost-in-the-middle and recency on the harm side; k=7 S1@7 vs S7@7 for context length; the natural similarity order O on MIXED-LATE games (same-type item at natural rank 2 or 3, where O coincides with S2 or S3) versus S1 as the derived type-aware reordering gain; static3 from Measurement C as the type-level reference for absolute credits; composed-vs-natural MIXED sets, task type, natural rank of the same-type item and item token counts as covariates.
Falsifiable Predictions: Design half-widths (95%, cluster bootstrap over games) are calibrated from Measurement C, where 548 paired cells gave +/-5.3 net for a content contrast; order contrasts on an identical item set have at most that variance: 1,600 paired cells +/-3, 1,280 +/-3.5, 1,200 +/-3.5, 800 +/-4.5. Every threshold pair below is separated by at least twice the design half-width, so the predicted and the falsifying outcome give non-overlapping CIs; an observed value between them is reported as inconclusive, not as support. P1 (ALL-SAME, O vs R, 200 games x 6 seeds, 1,200 cells): f(R) - f(O) is equivalent to zero within +/-5 net by two one-sided tests at 5% (the 90% CI lies inside (-5, +5), which at this power requires |f(R) - f(O)| <= 2 observed). Falsified if |f(R) - f(O)| >= 8 net, the CI then lying outside the band: order matters even among consistent items. Not entailed: primacy or recency can act on consistent items, and reversal moves the most-similar item to the last slot. P2, headline (MIXED forced-slot, 200 games x 8 seeds, 1,600 cells, +/-3): f(S1) - f(S3) >= +8 net. Falsified if <= +2 net (slot-invariant reader; the CI then excludes +8). This contrast is by construction the slot component of the same-type item's LOO credit and is reported in absolute net with its CI. P3 (PROC planted, 160 games x 8 seeds, 1,280 cells, +/-3.5): harm(slot 1) - harm(slot 3) = f(C3) - f(C1) >= +8 net. Falsified if <= +1 net, including any negative value (recency dominance). P4 (same cells): the premium is a slot-1 step: D12 = f(C2) - f(C1) >= +7 net and D23 = f(C3) - f(C2) >= -1 net. Falsified if D12 <= 0 (no step between slot 1 and slot 2; a P3 premium, if present, is then a slot-3 discount rather than first-exposure adoption) or if D23 <= -8 (slot 2 is the safest slot: lost-in-the-middle). P5 (k=7, MIXED, 200 games x 4 seeds, 800 cells, +/-4.5): f(S1@7) - f(S7@7) >= +9 net. Falsified if <= 0 (the premium vanishes with longer context). P6 (MIXED S1 vs S2, 200 games x 6 seeds, 1,200 cells, +/-3.5): f(S1) - f(S2) >= +7 net (the help-side premium is also a slot-1 step). Falsified if <= 0 (slot 2 is as good as slot 1; the P2 premium is then a slot-3 penalty). Not entailed by P2, which fixes S1 - S3 and says nothing about where S2 lies between them. Derived and reported with CIs but not pre-registered: the type-aware reordering gain f(S1) - f(O) on MIXED-LATE games and the corrected nested-k per-position profile.
Measurement and Noise Control: All contrasts are within (game, seed) on an identical item set, so content and type credit are held fixed by construction and the static3 credit of Measurement C cancels inside every slot contrast; absolute credits (S1 - k0 and S1 - static3 on validation MIXED games, from the k-sweep and Measurement C logs) are reported against the measured +17.2 residual. Pools are fixed before rollout from retrieval alone and sized from the MDE: 1,600 cells for the headline (+/-3), 1,280 for the planted arm (+/-3.5), 1,200 for the ALL-SAME and S2 arms (+/-3.5), 800 for k=7 (+/-4.5); thresholds sit at twice the half-width. Cluster bootstrap over games (seeds nested in games) for all CIs; a permutation test over run labels within (game, seed) plus TOST for P1. Name: stage_conditional_item_value
Title: The Same Item, Three Moments: Stage-Conditional Counterfactual Value of Retrieved Experience in Multi-Step Agents
Short Hypothesis: A retrieved item's counterfactual value depends on when in the episode it is consumed. Injected at the step where the procedure is due, a procedure-bound item (top-1 expert trajectory or the static type-conditioned exemplars) retains its entry-stage value within the measurement floor, even in the games the no-memory reader never reaches pickup; injected at a recovery point after the reader is stuck, a same-type expert item whose trajectory is location-mismatched with the current game becomes net harmful while a location-matched one still helps, and the matched item buffers the mismatched one non-additively; across same-type candidate classes the class x stage interaction is at least as large a component of per-(class, game) value as class identity, so per-item scores learned at entry lose their rank signal at recovery.
Related Work: Retrieval timing is a design choice in agent memory systems: SLEA-RL retrieves at each decision step conditioned on observation clusters and assigns step-level credit to actions, not items (2603.18079); MERIT argues memory usefulness changes across interaction stages and learns episode- and turn-level retrieval policies with PRM proxy rewards (2606.00547); U-EHR combines step-level credit with UCB-guided retrieval (KDD 2026). MemHarness shows verbatim replay of retrieved experience causes negative transfer and trains a reconstruction policy, without attributing the harm to items or stages (2607.28272); UCOB finds skills mislead in some states and credits the skill-conditioned prompt as a whole (2606.29502); memory anchoring is measured as an aggregate dependence dimension (2601.05107); the compliance trap locates harm at the first exposed decision point (2607.10608). Home literature on action advising values advice by the state in which it is given - when-to-advise budgets (2211.07882), intervention timing (2502.04576), state importance (2404.08828), teacher bridges at high-disagreement states (2608.01953) - but for policy training, never for the same retrieved item injected at controlled points of a common prefix with a paired counterfactual. Archived action_prior_imprinting and dormant_is_not_dead are adjacent on priors and pruning, not on within-episode timing.
Abstract: Per-item utility scores are stage-free numbers, yet the value an item adds plausibly depends on what the agent has already done. We measure the counterfactual value of the same ALFWorld item injected at three moments of the same (game, seed) episode: entry (step 0), procedure-due (the first step after the target object is in hand, reached by replaying the reader's own no-memory prefix or, where that prefix never reaches pickup, the environment's expert plan) and recovery (the first step after a pre-registered stuck signal in the no-memory run, harvested over 8 seeds so the recovery cell is as large as the entry cell). ALFWorld is deterministic given the game file, so a prefix is replayed without LLM calls and continued with or without an injected item; the paired contrast at each stage is a stage-conditional leave-one-out with fresh sampling in both arms. Item classes are manufactured for power: same-type expert top-1, same-type location-mismatched, same-type location-matched, the best static arm of Measurement C (static3) as the type-level control, and a cross-type token-matched placebo; set arms at recovery and at entry give the pairwise-minus-single removal interaction. We decompose headroom-normalized per-(class, game) value into class, stage and interaction components with a symmetric comparison, test whether entry-trained per-item scores keep their pair-level rank signal at recovery under matched sample sizes, and report the re-run cost of a stage-indexed value table relative to a stage-free one. The contribution is a measurement of how much of an item's value is a property of the moment rather than of the item, and where a stage-free score fails.
Experiments: Setting: ALFWorld valid (274 games), Qwen3-32B reader on two vLLM replicas (one per A100), expert bank of train trajectories, paired contrasts on the same (game, seed, prefix), 20 episodes/min with both replicas busy. T0 (prefix source): k=0 runs with full action traces on 8 seeds (2,192; the 2 sweep seeds reused where traces exist, 6 regenerated = 1,644). Stages, pre-registered: S0 = step 0. S1 = first step after 'You pick up the {obj}'; stratum A (k=0 run reached pickup) replays the reader's own k=0 prefix; stratum B (k=0 run never reached pickup) replays the ALFWorld expert plan (extra.expert_plan) up to and including the pickup, so every (game, seed) has an S1 and the games that need navigation help stay in the comparison; strata reported separately and pooled. S2 = first step of the k=0 run at which the last 3 actions were non-progress ('Nothing happens.' or re-examining a receptacle already examined without state change); pre-registered ladder: if 8 seeds yield fewer than 1,096 S2 prefixes, the rung drops to 2 non-progress actions; rung used and excluded counts reported (expected 55-65% of runs at rung 1, ~1,300 prefixes). Injection: replay the prefix in the env (no LLM calls), then continue with the item appended to the prompt as retrieved experience; the paired 'without' arm is a fresh no-item continuation from the same prefix with a new sampling seed so both arms carry sampling noise; the original k=0 continuation is a free second no-item sample used for the noise floor. Item classes, per game: I1 same-type expert top-1 by similarity; I2 same-type expert whose pick receptacle type differs from the current game's (location-mismatched); I3 same-type expert whose pick and target receptacle types match (location-matched; games without such an item excluded and counted); I4 = static3, the best static arm of Measurement C (3 fixed type-conditioned exemplars, +12.4 over k0 at entry); I5 cross-type token-matched placebo. T1 (S0): I1-I5 x 4 seeds = 5 x 1,096 full episodes, 'without' = the k=0 run at the same seed. T2 (S1): I1-I4 + fresh no-item, 5 x 1,096 partials. T3 (S2): I1-I5 + fresh no-item, 6 x ~1,300 partials. T4 (composition at S2): {I1,I2,I3}, {I1,I3}, {I1,I2} on all S2 prefixes, 3 x ~1,300 partials, with {I1} taken from T3; T4' (composition at S0): the same 3 set arms on 2 seeds, 3 x 548 full. T5 (scorers): outcome-reinforced and usage-decay per-item scores trained on a k=3 stream of 600 held-out train games x 1 seed (no valid-game leakage); offline confidence gain (reader logprob gain of its first action with vs without the item) and similarity to the task text as stage-free per-(item, query) scores; similarity to the current observation at S2 as the state-conditioned comparison. A1 reconstruction control at S2 (item rewritten by the reader to the current observation, MemHarness-style) for I2/I3 on 1 seed, 2 x ~325 partials; A2 reader swap at S2 (Qwen3-14B on one replica) for I2/I3/no-item on 1 seed, 3 x ~325 partials; A3 stuck-rung ablation (the unused rung) for I2/I3/no-item on 1 seed, 3 x ~325 partials. Budget (partials at 0.6 of an episode; S2 continuations are shorter, so this is an upper bound): T0 1,644 + T1 5,480 + T2 3,288 + T3 4,680 + T4 2,340 + T4' 1,644 + T5 600 + A1 390 + A2 585 + A3 585 = 21,236 episode-equivalents, ~17.7 h at 20 episodes/min with both replicas busy, one nohup job per phase with resumable JSONL; T0 and T5 run on one replica while the 50-game determinism check and T1 start on the other. Stage definitions, class rules, thresholds and MDEs pre-registered before T1.

Not entailed: a procedure-bound entry gain can still be spent before pickup (the item's trajectory reveals where the object is), and stratum B is exactly where that help is needed. Falsified if I2's CI includes zero or is positive (mismatch is not harmful at recovery), or if the DiD's CI includes zero (mismatch is an item property, not a stage property); produced by T3 and T1 for I2/I3. P3 (headline, interaction vs identity): two-way decomposition of headroom-normalized per-(class, game) value (net divided by the no-item failure rate at that stage on the same prefix set), intersection subset with all three stages defined, over I1-I4 x {S0, S1, S2}, noise-corrected components (sampling variance from the no-item vs no-item pairs subtracted), game-level bootstrap: the class x stage interaction component is >= the class main-effect component. Falsified if the bootstrap CI of (interaction - class) lies entirely below zero; this outcome is reachable if I2's harm and the static-vs-retrieved gap are stage-invariant. Stage main vs class main, the raw-scale decomposition and the I1-I5 table (S0/S2) are reported as secondary; produced by T1-T3. P4 (stage-free scores lose rank signal at recovery): pair-level Spearman between each scorer's score of the injected item and the paired contrast outcome (with minus without, in {-1, 0, +1}) on I1-I3 pairs pooled (~3,300 per stage), S0 pairs subsampled to the S2 count on the same games (100 subsamples): rho_S0 >= 0.10 for at least one scorer (positive control; if none, P4 is void, not confirmed) and rho_S0 - rho_S2 >= 0.10 with CI excluding zero for the outcome-reinforced scorer (MDE ~0.05). Falsified if the difference's CI includes zero for the outcome-reinforced scorer or rho_S2 >= rho_S0; produced by T5 against T1/T3. Reported alongside: whether state-conditioned similarity recovers at least half the gap. P5 (non-additivity at recovery): interaction = [v({I1,I2,I3}) - v({I1,I3})] - [v({I1,I2}) - v({I1})] at S2, ~1,300 prefixes per arm, MDE ~8: >= +8 (I2's harm is at least halved when I3 is present). Falsified if the interaction's CI includes zero (additive) or its upper bound is below +8; produced by T4 with T3's {I1} arm. The same interaction at S0 (T4', 548, MDE ~12) is reported as the composition-by-stage contrast, not predicted. Positive controls before any null in P3-P5 is reported: I1 at S0 reproduces k1 - k0 (+12.4 + 9.1 = +21.5) within CI, I4 at S0 reproduces +12.4 within CI, and the I3 >= +8 half of P2 holds.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired contrasts on the same (game, seed, prefix): at S0 the 'without' arm is the k=0 run at that seed; at S1/S2 it is a fresh no-item continuation, with the original k=0 continuation as a second free no-item sample giving the noise floor (no-item vs no-item) at each stage. Cell sizes and CIs (net success points, game-level bootstrap, seed blocking): S0 1,096 (+/-5.7), S1 1,096 (+/-5.7; stratum B ~770, +/-6.8), S2 ~1,300 (+/-5.2); within-stage class gaps +/-7.4 to +/-8; cross-stage differences paired by game (per-game means over seeds) +/-5.7 (S0-S1, pooled I1+I4 at 2,192 per stage) and +/-11 (DiD, I2/I3); the four-arm interaction +/-8 at S2 and +/-12 at S0. Every threshold in the predictions is set at or above the corresponding MDE, and MDEs are re-derived from realized cell sizes before unblinding. Headroom normalization (net divided by the no-item failure rate at that stage on the same prefix set) so a shorter remaining horizon cannot manufacture an interaction; raw-scale results reported alongside. Variance components noise-corrected by subtracting the sampling variance estimated from the no-item vs no-item pairs, bootstrap CIs on the corrected components. Stage selection handled by within-stage pairing, by reporting excluded-game counts per stage and rung, and by running the primary decomposition on the intersection subset with full-subset values alongside. Scorer analyses at the (item, game, seed) pair level with S0 subsampled to the S2 count on the same games, so differential reliability cannot produce the sign; split-half reliability of each stage's class-value table reported. Estimator cost as estimand: re-runs per class for a stable class rank at each stage (rank stability across bootstrap resamples) for the stage-indexed vs the stage-free table, LLM-call cost including partial-episode savings, throughput per replica (episodes/min, tok/s).
