Name: item_credit_variance_decomposition
Title: Is There an Item to Credit? Between-Item Variance, Re-run Cost and the Winner's Curse of Per-Item Counterfactual Credit in an ALFWorld Experience Bank
Short Hypothesis: Within a class of same-type expert items the true between-item SD of leave-one-out credit is below 5 net points, indistinguishable from zero at 64 paired re-runs per item, so per-item scores over an expert bank fit re-run noise; item-level signal exists only between classes (expert vs self-written vs planted-wrong) and within self-written items, whose between-item SD is at least 12 net. Consequently even a half-reliable per-item rank (split-half 0.5) of self-written items needs about 18 paired re-runs per half and a 0.8-reliable one about 72 per half (about 145 per item), top-quartile selection on 4 re-runs is at least 65% illusory, and pruning by per-item credit recovers planted-wrong items with precision above 0.55 only at 16 or more re-runs per item; the item signal among self-written items is reader-general (its rank transfers to a second backbone), whereas no expert-item rank exists to transfer.
Related Work: Data Shapley (arxiv:1904.02868) and Data Banzhaf (arxiv:2205.15466, verified) show that leave-one-out and Shapley data values are unstable under stochastic training and that the Banzhaf value is the noise-robust semivalue; SCARV (arxiv:2605.00944) studies stable sample ranking under redundancy; FreeShap (arxiv:2406.04606) and amortized Shapley (arxiv:2305.19998) cut the cost of instance attribution. None decomposes item value into a between-item component and a re-run noise component, and none concerns retrieved experience consumed by an agent. On the agent side, TreeMem (arxiv:2605.04811) Monte-Carlo-averages branches without stating how many are needed, Shapley-RAG (arxiv:2507.04480) does not report attribution stability across repeated calls, HiMPO (arxiv:2606.16285) and AttriMem (arxiv:2607.21106) do not report the sample cost of their local utilities, and every scorer family (MemQ arxiv:2605.08374, RoMeRL arxiv:2608.02508, SF-AMS arxiv:2607.22562) presumes that items within a bank differ in value. The reliability-versus-re-run curve (Spearman-Brown) and disattenuation are classical test theory; no data-valuation or memory paper reports them for an item value. The archived counterfactual_memory_screening_under_selection_noise assumed a noise model; the archived memory_item_value_reliability had no intervention arm.
Abstract: Per-item utility scores are the target of every self-evolving memory system, yet no one has asked whether same-class items in a bank differ in counterfactual value by more than the noise of measuring it. We take 100 items from the ALFWorld bank (40 expert, 40 self-pool successes, 20 planted wrong-procedure derivatives, stratified by task type), force each into a k=3 retrieved set on a fixed 16-game panel of its type, and run FULL versus minus-item on every (game, seed) with a Qwen3-32B reader: 4 seeds for expert items (64 paired re-runs per item), 2 for the others. Per-item credit is decomposed at the item-mean level into a class mean, a between-item SD in net points and re-run noise, with a planted-spread nominal class (expert plus wrong pooled) as the check that the estimator detects spread when it exists. The same cell, split by games and separately by seeds, gives the reliability-versus-re-run curve, the winner's-curse retention of selected items compared with the retention the variance components imply, and the precision with which a bottom-quantile pruning rule recovers the planted-wrong items at 4, 16 and 32 re-runs. A second composition (item plus cross-type items), a pairwise-removal additivity cell, a token-matched replacement arm and a consumer-swap arm on a second backbone with its own retrieval positive control bound the estimand; a one-forward-pass confidence-gain proxy is placed on the same reliability-cost curve. The result is the prerequisite every scorer paper skips: whether there is an item-level quantity to learn inside a class, and what it costs to measure.
Experiments: Items: 40 expert E (about 7 per type over 6 ALFWorld types), 40 self-pool successes S (same types, success-filtered on-policy), 20 planted-wrong W (procedure action swapped in 20 of the E items, e.g. heat -> cool, same object and receptacle). Games: per type a fixed 16-game panel from valid_seen+valid_unseen (96 games), shared by every item of that type, so game effects are estimable and split-halves use the same games for every item; an item qualifies if its natural retrieval rank is <= 20 on at least 12 panel games (rank logged as a covariate). Two co-retrieved-set compositions: C1 (natural) = item at position 1 plus the game's top-2 natural same-type expert items, HOLE = those two alone (k=2); C2 (isolated) = item plus two fixed cross-type expert items, HOLE = the two cross-type items, so in C2 the item is the only same-type procedure carrier. Cells (episodes = items x games x seeds x arms): (1) C1 main, the decision cell: E 40 x 16 x 4 seeds x 2 = 5,120 (64 paired re-runs per item, per-item SE 6.4 net); S 40 x 16 x 2 x 2 = 2,560 (32 paired, SE 9.0); W 20 x 16 x 2 x 2 = 1,280 (32 paired); subtotal 8,960. (2) C2 composition: 16 E + 16 W + 8 S x 8 games x 2 seeds x 2 = 1,280 (320 paired per class for E and W, +/-5.6 net). (3) Additivity in C1: 12 E + 8 S + 4 W x 8 games x 2 seeds x 2 extra arms (co-item e2 removed; item and e2 both removed) = 768, tested against the sum of the two single removals at class level. (4) Token-matched replacement (the rank-4 same-type expert of length within +/-15%) for 20 E x 8 games x 2 seeds = 320. (5) Consumer swap on backbone 2: S 40 x 8 x 2 x 2 = 1,280; E 20 + W 20 x 8 x 2 x 2 = 1,280; per-backbone positive control k3 vs k0 on the 96 panel games x 2 seeds = 384; subtotal 2,944. Total 14,272 episodes, about 12 h at 20 episodes/min on two vLLM replicas (one per A100, workers tuned to the running queue); if the envelope is tighter the drop order is C2's S sub-cell, then cell (3), then the fourth E seed (which raises P1's MDE from 5 to about 5.5 net). k0/static3/k3 on the panel games for backbone 1 come from the Measurement C logs (paired per game), giving the static-net reference at no cost. Proxy: first-procedure-action log-probability shift with vs without the item on the identical prompts (forward passes only); nested-k slot credit from existing logs. Order: cell (1) runs seeds-first: W and E at seeds 1-2 first (P3 and the estimator gate on the pooled E+W class), thresholds pre-registered, then S and the remaining E seeds, then (2)-(5). Analyses: per-item credit c_i = mean paired contrast (FULL - HOLE, net points) with SE_i; item-level heteroscedastic random-effects model (REML, and method of moments tau^2 = var(c_i) - mean SE_i^2) per class giving the between-item SD tau_class in net points with parametric-bootstrap CIs over items and games; reliability R(m) = tau^2/(tau^2 + sigma^2/m) with sigma the per-re-run residual SD (about 51 net from the prior arms); split-half Spearman across items from disjoint game halves (game-split) and from disjoint seed sets on the same games (seed-split) at m in {4, 8, 16, 32} paired re-runs per half, 200 random halvings, item bootstrap for CIs; winner's curse: top (or bottom) quantile by half A, half-B excess over the pool mean divided by half-A excess, compared with R(m); pruning: precision of the bottom-quantile rule against the planted-wrong labels at each m, and for the self-pool the half-B deficit of the half-A bottom 20%; reliability-cost curve (LLM calls at each reliability) for HOLE credit, the proxy and nested-k slot credit.
Baselines and Ablations: Class-mean model (tau = 0) vs item random-effect model as the likelihood-ratio test of P1, with the pooled E+W nominal class as the estimator's positive control; expert vs self-written vs planted-wrong classes; composition C1 (natural, item plus two same-type experts) vs C2 (isolated, item plus two cross-type experts), with class means and tau re-estimated in C2; additivity: pairwise removal (item and co-item e2) vs the sum of the two single removals at class level, and the Banzhaf-style two-coalition average of the item's credit; hole vs token-matched replacement for expert items (slot credit vs item credit); static-procedure reference: the C1 HOLE set already contains two same-type expert exemplars (the static3 content), so C1 credit is net of type-procedure credit by construction, and C2 credit is reported net of static3 - k0 = +12.4 and as a fraction of k3 - static3 = +17.2 from the Measurement C logs on the same panel games; confidence-gain proxy and nested-k slot credit as cheaper estimators on the reliability-cost curve; seeds as a nested factor (seed-split vs game-split reliability); second backbone as a separate consumer-swap arm with its own k3 vs k0 positive control; random pruning (precision 0.33 in the E+W sub-pool, 0.20 in the full pool, by composition) as the decision baseline.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (headline, no within-class item signal for expert items): in composition C1 the between-item SD of true credit among same-type expert items, tau_E, is below 5 net with 95% bootstrap CI upper bound below 8 net. Arm: 40 E x 16 panel games x 4 seeds, FULL vs HOLE (64 paired re-runs per item, per-item SE 6.4 net, error variance 41 net^2). Falsified if tau_E >= 8 net with CI lower bound > 4 net: expert items whose true values differ by 8 net give an observed between-item variance of item means of about 105 against 41 under the null, 6.9 null-SEs apart (relative SE 0.23 at 40 items), so this outcome is reachable and distinguishable; the inconclusive band is tau_E in (5, 8) and is reported as such. Gate before scoring: the same estimator applied to the pooled E+W nominal class (spread planted by P3's separation, expected about 7 net at a 15-net separation) must return tau >= 5 net with CI excluding 0.
- P2 (self-written items carry item signal): tau_S >= 12 net with CI lower bound > 5 net, and tau_S - tau_E >= 6 net with bootstrap CI excluding 0. Arm: 40 S x 16 x 2 seeds (32 paired, SE 9.0, error variance 81). Falsified if tau_S <= 5 net with CI upper bound < 10 net (self-written successes are as interchangeable as expert ones): under tau_S = 5 the observed variance is 106 +/- 24 and the tau CI upper bound about 8.5 net, so the falsifier is reachable.
- P3 (positive control, run first): W - E class-mean separation in C1 >= 15 net (W 640 paired +/-3.9, E at two seeds 1,280 paired +/-2.7, difference +/-5). Falsified if < 8 net; the reachable failure is a reader that ignores the planted-wrong item in favour of its two correct co-items (Measurement C's wrong-type placebo cost only -3 net under k0, and C1 bounds any single item's credit by k3 - k2, about 4 net); then C2 (the item is the sole same-type carrier, expected separation about 25 net) becomes the primary composition and all thresholds are re-registered before any other claim.
- P4 (re-runs for a stable rank): within the self-pool class the game-split split-half Spearman is <= 0.25 at m = 4 paired re-runs per half and between 0.35 and 0.6 at m = 16 (R_S(m) = tau_S^2/(tau_S^2 + sigma^2/m) with tau_S = 12, sigma = 51 gives 0.18 and 0.47), so by Spearman-Brown a half-reliable rank needs about 18 paired re-runs per half and a 0.8-reliable one about 72 per half (about 145 per item, 4.5x this study's per-item budget); the expert curve is reported but scored under P1. Falsified if the self-pool split-half is >= 0.5 at m = 4 (requires tau_S >= 25 net, a heavy-tailed self pool) or <= 0.15 at m = 16 with item-bootstrap CI excluding 0.35. Second clause: seed-split and game-split Spearman at equal m agree within 0.1 in every class; falsified if the seed-split exceeds the game-split by >= 0.2 in any class (an item x game interaction: item value is game-specific and no game-general item rank exists, which mis-specifies the additive model rather than underpowering it). Arm: C1 cell, 200 halvings; E's 4 seeds give the seed-split at m = 32.
- P5 (winner's curse tracks the variance components): top-quartile self-pool items (10 of 40) selected on half A at m = 4 retain <= 35% of their half-A excess on half B (selection on 4 re-runs is >= 65% illusory) and 35-60% at m = 16; in every class and in the pooled 100-item pool (top and bottom decile) observed retention is within +/-0.15 of R(m) implied by the P1/P2 components. Falsified if self-pool retention at m = 4 is >= 0.5 (tau_S >= 25 net), or if in any cell observed retention departs from R(m) by >= 0.25 in either direction (a heavy-tailed or bimodal item distribution, e.g. a few catastrophic self-written items, makes selection more real than additive-normal components allow; an item x game interaction makes it less). The pooled pool, whose spread is planted by W, is the cell in which high retention is reachable (R_pool(16) about 0.4). Arm: C1 split-half, 200 halvings, effective SE about 0.1 per retention estimate (item bootstrap).
- P6 (re-runs a pruning decision needs): in the 60-item E+W sub-pool, pruning the bottom third by credit from m paired re-runs recovers planted-wrong items with precision <= 0.55 at m = 4 (random pruning 0.33; expected 0.49 at a 15-net separation), >= 0.55 at m = 16 and >= 0.65 at m = 32 (expected 0.62 and 0.72); within the self-pool class, the bottom 20% by half-A credit at m = 16 has half-B credit >= 6 net below the class mean (8 items x 16 paired = 128 paired per halving, SE 4.5 net; expected deficit about 11 net). Falsified if precision >= 0.6 at m = 4 (separation >= 30 net or sigma well below 51: wrong items are far easier to spot than the noise model says and per-item pruning is cheap), or <= 0.45 at m = 32, or if the self-pool pruned set's half-B deficit has bootstrap CI upper bound < 3 net (no reader-general bad self-written items). Precision over 200 game-subset draws has effective SE about 0.06. Arm: C1 cell with planted labels as ground truth; the 100-item pool precision (where genuinely bad self items compete for the bottom) is reported descriptively.
- P7 (consumer swap, separate arm): gate: on backbone 2, k3 - k0 on the 96 panel games x 2 seeds (192 paired, +/-7) is >= 10 net; if < 5 net the swap cell is declared uninterpretable (reader ignores retrieval, or serving/prompt-format failure) and P7 is not scored. Given the gate: (a) the W - E separation on backbone 2 is within +/-8 net of backbone 1's (20 E + 20 W x 8 games x 2 seeds, 320 paired per class, +/-5.6); falsified if < 5 net while the gate holds (the reader uses retrieval but recovers from a wrong procedure through environment feedback). (b) tau_S on backbone 2 >= 8 net with CI lower bound > 4 (40 S x 8 x 2, 16 paired per item, error variance 163); falsified if <= 4 net with CI upper bound < 8 (the self-pool spread is reader-specific). (c) the cross-backbone Spearman of per-item credit over the 40 S items is >= 0.3 (attenuation ceiling sqrt(R1 R2) about 0.55 at tau_S = 12 with 32 and 16 paired re-runs); falsified if <= 0 (SE about 0.16 at 40 items, one-sided test against 0.3): item quality among self-written items does not transfer between readers.
Measurement and Noise Control: Each (item, game, seed) contributes one paired binary contrast in {-1, 0, +1} with residual SD sigma about 51 net (SE 9 net at 32 paired re-runs in the prior arms); per-item SE is 6.4 net at 64, 9.0 at 32 and 12.7 at 16 paired re-runs, which is why no claim is made about a single item and the estimands are between-item SDs, reliabilities, class means and label-recovery rates. Power: the between-item variance of item means is estimated with relative SE about sqrt(2/39) = 0.23 at 40 items; at 64 re-runs the null value is 41 net^2, so tau = 5 net (V = 66) is 2.7 null-SEs above the null and tau = 8 net (V = 105) is 6.9 above; the MDE for tau_E at 80% power is about 5 net and the inconclusive band tau_E in (5, 8) is stated. Class means: W 640 paired (+/-3.9 net), E at two seeds 1,280 (+/-2.7), difference +/-5; C2 and swap class cells at 320 paired (+/-5.6). Variance components near the boundary are estimated by REML and by method of moments with parametric bootstrap over items and games, both reported. Split-half statistics are averaged over 200 random halvings with item-bootstrap CIs; seeds nested in games; the same game panel for every item of a type so game effects cancel in rank statistics; the estimator gate (pooled E+W class must show tau >= 5 net with CI excluding 0) is passed before P1 is scored; retrieval is controlled (every item has exactly the stated number of re-runs on the same games), removing the retrieval-frequency confound; prompt hashes, item ids, natural retrieval rank and token count logged; the proxy is computed on identical prompts; both GPUs serve one replica each with workers tuned to the vLLM running queue (>= 8 per replica); thresholds of P1-P7 pre-registered after the P3 cell.

Name: pairwise_removal_interaction_audit
Title: Removal Is Not Additive: Interaction, Copy Count and Seed Cost of Per-Item Credit on Natural and Manufactured Retrieved Sets in a Multi-Step Agent
Short Hypothesis: In ALFWorld with a Qwen3-32B reader and k=3 retrieval, the counterfactual value of a retrieved item is not an item property: it depends on what is co-retrieved with it, and it does so often enough in the retriever's own sets that per-item credit is estimator-dependent. Three claims, each with a named refuting arm. (i) NATURAL (headline): on the retriever's own top-3 sets, single-removal (leave-one-out, LOO) credit and exact Shapley credit computed on disjoint seed halves agree less than two LOO estimates agree with each other, and LOO's top item differs from Shapley's in >= 20% of sets net of the seed-noise floor; a rank-1-dominated, additive retrieval distribution (cross-estimator agreement at least as high as within-estimator agreement) refutes it. (ii) SIGN: on manufactured pairs beside a natural third item, the pairwise interaction I(a,b) = f(S) - f(S-a) - f(S-b) + f(S-ab) on the same (game, seed) is negative for a correct plus a planted conflicting same-type procedure (the wrong item dominates and masks the correct item's value; additive reconciliation gives I ~ 0 and correct-item rescue gives a positive I the size of the wrong item's harm), positive for two complementary fragments, and zero within a pre-registered equivalence bound for a cross-type control. (iii) DOSE: copy count is inert: two content-identical paraphrase copies of the rank-1 item add <= +2 net over the item alone, so the +8 net that natural items 2-3 add over item 1 (Measurement C: k3 - k1) is content, not repetition; amplification of >= +8 net refutes it. The number of seeds at which a per-item removal rank stabilizes is an estimand measured on 8-seed split halves, not a footnote.
Related Work: CUE-R (arxiv:2604.05467) measures REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE per evidence item in single-shot RAG and reports non-additive multi-hop interactions, but no multi-step agent, no pairwise-removal estimand and no run-to-run variance or cost. Shapley source attribution in RAG (arxiv:2507.04480) compares SHAP approximations to exact document attributions under redundancy/complementarity/synergy on QA, without stochastic-evaluation noise or agents. The scaffold-level 2^5 factorial (arxiv:2605.05716) finds 56% submodularity violations among components, not among retrieved items. DG-Mem (arxiv:2608.23268) uses Shapley context attribution over memory entries as a component of a multimodal agentic learner and does not test additivity or estimator noise. RoMeRL (arxiv:2608.02508) posits contamination of co-retrieved memories by jointly assigned rewards without a counterfactual check; MemQ (arxiv:2605.08374) leaves credit splitting among co-retrieved siblings open. The compliance trap (arxiv:2607.10608) shows early adoption of conflicting memory but never varies the co-retrieved set. Formal home: Shapley interaction indices (shapiq arxiv:2410.01649; joint Shapley arxiv:2107.11357). Archived: counterfactual_memory_screening_under_selection_noise (5.45) assumed its interference and noise model; retrieved_set_disagreement_gate (4.65) claimed set-level harm without item-level ground truth. This proposal measures interference with the pairwise cell on manufactured classes and on the retriever's own sets, copy count with a content-held-fixed dose arm (CUE-R's DUPLICATE is its single-shot nearest neighbour), and estimator noise with no-op repeats and disjoint seed halves, with stated power per cell.
Abstract: Every self-evolving memory system scores its items, but a per-item score is meaningful only if an item's value is an item property. We test the weakest form of that assumption, additivity of removal effects, in a multi-step agent, and we test it where it matters: on the sets the retriever actually returns. On ALFWorld with a Qwen3-32B reader and k=3 retrieval from the expert bank we run, on the same (game, seed), the full 2^3 subset lattice of the natural top-3 set plus a no-op repeat, and compute leave-one-out (LOO) and exact Shapley credit on disjoint seed halves. The headline estimand is the excess of cross-estimator over within-estimator disagreement: under additivity Shapley equals LOO cell by cell and, being less noisy, can only agree better, so any excess is interaction in the wild. Mechanism cells manufacture the interaction classes beside a natural third item (correct + planted conflicting procedure; two complementary fragments; helpful + cross-type control) and predict class-specific signs, with the conflict cell framed as a dominance test whose refuting outcome (the correct item rescues the harmed baseline, I positive) is as reachable as its confirming one. A dose arm holds content fixed and varies copy count (one versus three paraphrase copies of the rank-1 item, and of a procedure-deleted degraded copy) to decide whether the measured +8 net marginal value of items 2-3 is content or repetition. An 8-seed subsample gives the split-half reliability of per-item credit as a function of seed count and the LLM-call cost of LOO versus Shapley at matched reliability. Item credit is reported net of Measurement C's static3 arm and under a second background. The result is a measured rather than assumed interference model that says how often per-item credit in an experience bank is well-defined, which estimator to trust, and what a reliable estimate costs in re-runs.
Experiments: (1) Materials: expert bank; k-sweep retrieval logs (runs/sweep/k_sweep_final.jsonl) for the valid games and the same retriever applied to bank-disjoint train-stream games; Qwen3-32B reader on two vLLM replicas (one per GPU, clients spread across both). Games: all procedure-bound types (clean/heat/cool) in valid_seen+valid_unseen (~140) plus ~160 bank-disjoint train-stream games of the same types (partition verified before pre-registration) = 300 games. Natural items r1, r2, r3 = the retriever's rank 1-3 for the game. Cell tiers, nested so subsets are shared across arms: Tier A = 300 games x 6 seeds = 1,800 paired cells (+/-3.5 net); Tier N = 200 of those games (140 valid + 60 train-stream) x 6 seeds = 1,200 cells (+/-4 net); Tier B = the same 200 games x 4 seeds = 800 cells (+/-5 net); Tier S = 100 of the Tier N games x seeds 7-8 (with seeds 1-6 from Tier N, an 8-seed subsample). (2) Manufactured items, each token-matched to the item it replaces and placed in that item's retrieval-rank slot: p1, p2 = Qwen3-32B paraphrases of r1 with identical action sequence (exact action-string match after paraphrase); b_c = planted wrong-procedure item for the task type (clean: heats instead of using the sink; heat: uses the fridge; cool: uses the microwave); b_x = cross-type expert item; c1 = find-and-take fragment of a same-type expert episode cut before the procedure step, c2 = procedure-and-place fragment from another same-type episode with the same receptacle, jointly token-matched to one item; d = paraphrase of r1 with the procedure step deleted (find/take/place kept); f1, f2 = cross-type filler items (same construction as b_x); x' = natural cross-type item for the BACKGROUND arm. (3) Runs per (game, seed) cell, listing only non-shared runs. Name: hole_backfill_static_counterfactual
Title: Which Counterfactual Is Item Credit? Hole, Backfill and Static-Exemplar Replacement Give Different Per-Item Values for Retrieved Experience, and Only Backfill Predicts What Pruning Realizes
Short Hypothesis: For the same retrieved item in the same (game, seed) at the same slot, three references give three different credits: hole (the slot left empty; what CUE-R REMOVE, Shapley-RAG and DIG estimate), backfill (the retriever's next-ranked bank item enters in rank order; exactly what pruning the item from the bank realizes for that game) and static (the type's best static exemplar takes the slot; Measurement C at item level). For natural expert items at rank 1 the backfill recovers at least 8 net of the hole loss, so hole credit over-states the realized value of pruning by at least that much; the item still carries at least 8 net beyond the static exemplar (about half of the measured set residual k3 - static3 = +17.2 sits in the top slot), giving the ordering s(H1) < s(S1) < s(B1); and summed hole credits over-predict the realized loss of pruning two items by at least 12 net, while the summed-backfill error is reported against a pre-registered +/-10 margin. The hole-backfill gap is a slot property, identical for every item class by construction, so class enters only through the credit level: a planted wrong-procedure item at rank 1 has hole credit <= -10 net even with correct co-items, and both references prune it.
Related Work: CUE-R (arxiv:2604.05467) measures per-evidence utility by REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE in single-shot RAG, replacing with distractors rather than the retriever's own next candidate, and reports no cost or variance. Shapley source attribution in RAG (arxiv:2507.04480) and DIG confidence gain (arxiv:2509.12765) are hole-based marginal contributions in single-shot QA. The local additive attribution taxonomy (arxiv:2607.14271) names the reference (what replaces the removed input) as a specification choice but does not evaluate references against a downstream decision; semantic-missingness baselines (arxiv:2508.14482) argue the reference must be a plausible state, which for a memory bank is the next-ranked item. On the agent side credit is set-level (UCOB arxiv:2606.29502; ExpSuite arxiv:2605.30712), agent-level (TreeMem arxiv:2605.04811) or write-action-level (HiMPO arxiv:2606.16285); utility-refining systems that prune (ReMe arxiv:2512.10696; SF-AMS arxiv:2607.22562) never state which counterfactual their score is meant to track. Inside the program, the nested-k logs give hole credit per slot for free and Measurement C (runs/STEP0_RESULTS.md) fixes the best static arm (static3, three type-conditioned exemplars) and its set-level residual k3 - static3 = +17.2; nothing gives the backfill counterfactual, and no measurement puts the static content into a single slot with retrieved co-items present.
Abstract: Every memory system that prunes or admits items acts on a per-item score, but the score is validated (when at all) against removing the item and leaving a hole, whereas pruning realizes a different counterfactual: the retriever fills the slot with its next-ranked item. We measure, for the rank-1 item of the same ALFWorld (game, seed) with a Qwen3-32B reader over k=3 expert-bank sets, three references for the same slot: hole (k=2), backfill (the rank-4 item from the same k=7 retrieval log, in rank order, which is exactly what pruning that item from the bank re-retrieves for that game because retrieval is deterministic) and static (the static3 type-conditioned exemplar in the slot, Measurement C at item level). Each reference costs one re-run per (game, seed), the same as leave-one-out; 274 games x 6 seeds give +/-5 net on every two-arm paired contrast. Credits are reported under two co-retrieved-set compositions (natural, and with item 2 removed or pruned), for two item classes at the same slot (natural expert, planted wrong-procedure) with the shared counterfactual arms made explicit, and additivity is tested by pairwise versus single removal: the summed hole credits of items 1 and 2 are compared with the realized loss of pruning both (backfilled by items 4 and 5). The contribution is a statement of what per-item credit is for: the reference that equals what pruning realizes, its distance from hole credit and from static credit in net points, its additivity, its reader-dependence (separate consumer-swap arm), and the number of seeds a stable per-item rank needs under each reference.
Experiments: Unit: (game, seed) over the 274 valid_seen + valid_unseen games; 6 seeds for the core arms (1,644 units: +/-5 net on a two-arm paired contrast, +/-7 on a four-arm contrast), 4 seeds for the secondary arms (1,096 units: +/-5.7 / +/-8). Sets come from the k=7 logs in runs/sweep/k_sweep_final.jsonl (item ids in rank order; retrieval is deterministic, so removing items from the bank and re-retrieving for that game yields the next-ranked items in rank order, and the frozen log realizes per-game pruning exactly). Arms on natural expert sets, prompt order = rank order: F = [1,2,3]; H1 = [2,3]; B1 = [2,3,4]; S1 = [x,2,3] with x = the game's type-conditioned static3 exemplars, as many (1-3) as fall within 15% of item 1's token count (trimmed at a step boundary if needed; token ratio logged); H2 = [1,3]; B12 = [3,4,5]; H12 = [3]; B2 = [1,3,4]; F_w1 = [w,2,3] with w = item 1 with its procedure action swapped (heat<->cool, clean->heat) or its target receptacle swapped (pick types, look-in-light), token count within 5% of item 1. Credits c_X(p) = s(F) - s(X_p) paired by (game, seed); slot values g_1 = s(B1) - s(H1), sigma_1 = s(S1) - s(H1). Composition: c_H(1) is reported under [.,2,3] (F vs H1) and under [.,3] (H2 vs H12); c_B(1) under [.,2,3] (F vs B1) and under [.,3,4] (B2 vs B12). Pairwise vs single: hole sum c_H(1)+c_H(2) versus the realized two-item pruning loss s(F) - s(B12) (P3) and versus the pairwise hole c_H(12); backfill sum c_B(1)+c_B(2) versus s(F) - s(B12) (estimand D_B, margin +/-10). Class: F_w1 versus the same H1/B1 prompts (identical for every class; stated as such). Consumer swap: H1 and B1 re-run on the second local backbone (serving verified before the cell is scheduled). Budget: 6 arms x 1,644 (F, H1, B1, S1, H2, B12) = 9,864; 3 arms x 1,096 (H12, B2, F_w1) = 3,288; swap 2 arms x 1,096 = 2,192; total 15,344 episodes = 12.8 h at the measured 20 episodes/min on two vLLM replicas (one per A100, prefix caching on, episode workers raised until each replica's running queue stays >= 8), plus about 2% error re-runs; every arm is an append-only JSONL under nohup with a pid file. Order: F and H1 on seeds 1-4 first as the positive control (c_H(1) >= +10 at +/-5.7; if it fails, the pre-registered fallback makes the pair {1,2} the primary slot, with g_12 = s(B12) - s(H12) carrying P1 and the single-slot cells reported as exploratory); pre-registration of all thresholds filed before B1 starts; the remaining arms are interleaved across both replicas so neither GPU idles. If the confirmatory arms finish under budget, a bank-level realization arm R1 (prune every validation rank-1 item from the bank, re-retrieve, 1,644 episodes) runs on the remaining time as a fidelity estimand for s(B1) - s(R1); it carries no confirmatory prediction.
Baselines and Ablations: Nested-k slot credit from the existing logs (k=1 vs k=3 vs k=7) as the free position-level prior, which says items 4-7 add only +2 to +4 net on top of [1,2,3] and against which P1 is stated; k=1 leave-one-out excluded because it equals the k=0 contrast; hole vs backfill vs static as a within-unit factorial at the rank-1 slot; composition as a manipulated factor (each rank-1 credit under two co-sets: natural, and with item 2 removed or pruned); pairwise removal vs single removal for both references (P3 and the D_B estimand); class (natural expert vs planted wrong-procedure) at the same slot with the shared counterfactual arms made explicit; the static3 exemplar in the slot as the item-level Measurement C arm, with the set-level static3 numbers as the reference; backfill-to-removed-item similarity (embedding cosine, same-object flag, same-receptacle flag) as a covariate for g_1, separating near-duplicate backfills from distinct ones; per-type breakdown (clean/heat/cool vs pick types vs look-in-light) reported, not confirmatory; second backbone as a separate consumer-swap arm; seeds as a factor; split-half rank stability across seeds as the noise estimand.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (backfill differs from hole at rank 1; the mechanism): g_1 = s(B1) - s(H1) >= +8 net, i.e. the retriever's next candidate placed in the emptied rank-1 slot recovers at least 8 net of the hole loss, so hole credit over-states the value that pruning the item realizes by at least 8 net. Stated against the nested-k prior (items 4-7 add +2 to +4 on top of the full set). Falsified if g_1 <= 0 with the 95% CI excluding +8 (the next-ranked item adds nothing to [2,3]: hole credit is what pruning realizes and the reference does not matter). Arms: H1 vs B1, 1,644 paired, CI +/-5, MDE 7, band 8. The ratio c_B(1)/c_H(1) is reported with a bootstrap CI as an estimand under the gate c_H(1) >= +10, not as a target.

Name: per_item_loo_reliability_and_winners_curse
Title: How Many Retrievals Does a Memory Item Need? Measured Reliability, Winner's Curse and the Pruning Threshold of Per-Item Leave-One-Out Value
Short Hypothesis: For an ALFWorld bank of mixed provenance (expert items plus unfiltered self-written items) read by Qwen3-32B at k=3, the between-item variance of per-item leave-one-out (LOO) value is small relative to game x seed noise even though the bank visibly mixes good and poor items: a per-item rank needs tens of retrievals (split-half reliability below 0.5 at 12 retrievals per half), items selected as top-ranked keep at most half of their apparent excess on fresh re-runs and the loss is predicted out of sample by variance components fitted on disjoint games, LOO-score pruning beats random pruning only above a measured retrieval threshold, and much of what looks like item value is set value: it rises when a same-type neighbour is swapped for a neutral one, pair removal costs more than the sum of single removals, a static procedure prompt absorbs more of it at the item level than the measured +17.2 net set-level residual suggests, and a reader's ranking does not transfer to a second reader. Every quantity is measured by repeated intervention on fresh (game, seed) cells rather than assumed from a noise model.
Related Work: Data Shapley (arXiv:1904.02868) and leave-one-out valuation define item value as marginal utility for deterministic utilities and report no sample-size-to-reliability curve; Data Banzhaf (Wang and Jia 2023; not returned by the literature command, cited from memory) argues rank robustness under a stochastic utility but not for LLM re-runs. Source Attribution in RAG (arXiv:2507.04480) and CUE-R (arXiv:2604.05467) intervene per document in single-shot RAG and report neither seed variance nor re-run cost. Utility pruning and reweighting (ReMe arXiv:2512.10696; SF-AMS arXiv:2607.22562; RoMeRL arXiv:2608.02508) act on scores whose false-prune rates are unmeasured (G10, G24). Compound estimation for binomials (arXiv:2512.25042) and Scorio (arXiv:2603.10960) supply shrinkage and ranking tools for noisy per-unit binomial rates that we reuse offline; VIGOR (arXiv:2607.22002) allocates rollouts by reward variance and motivates the offline adaptive-allocation analysis. Archived counterfactual_memory_screening_under_selection_noise assumed its noise model; memory_item_value_reliability had no intervention arm; both are replaced here by measured variance components with LOO as ground truth, tested out of sample on disjoint games.
Abstract: Every self-evolving memory system scores its items, prunes the bottom and reinforces the top, yet no method reports how many retrievals a per-item value estimate needs before its rank is stable, nor how far the top-scored items regress when re-measured. We treat the noise of the per-item estimator as the estimand, and we measure it on a bank built to contain heterogeneity: expert items, about 200 unfiltered self-written items, 100 planted wrong-procedure items and 20 scene-matched solution items. With Qwen3-32B at k=3 we run leave-one-out re-runs for 1,200 train-stream games x 2 seeds (base plus three single removals), the stream chosen in a free offline retrieval pass so that a 120-item natural panel receives at least 24 retrievals per item in two game-disjoint halves. A crossed mixed model fitted on one game half predicts the split-half reliability and the winner's-curse shrinkage on the other half; both are compared with what is observed, so the noise model is tested rather than assumed. The decision-relevant claim is tested on held-out games screened offline so that every evaluation episode is one whose retrieved set the pruning actually changes: bottom-100 pruning by LOO score estimated from 6 or 24 retrievals per item, against random pruning of the same count (fresh draw per game) and oracle removal of the planted items, 2,200 paired episodes per arm. Composition is manipulated with a neutral token-matched cross-type swap and with named same-type pairs (pair removal versus the sum of single removals), a static3-augmented prompt measures item value net of static credit as a paired net-point drop, a second reader re-measures terciles ranked by the first reader, and a halved store re-measures the pooled single-removal effect. Cost is about 35,000 episodes (about 29 h on two replicas). The output is a retrievals-per-item requirement, an out-of-sample shrinkage factor for selected items, and a pruning threshold below which score-based pruning is indistinguishable from random pruning, each with a confidence interval and a sized falsifier.
Experiments: E0 (free, run first): nested-k position contrast from runs/sweep/k_sweep_final.jsonl (k=1 vs k=3 vs k=7 on the same games) gives per-position value and its game x seed spread; a 500-episode pilot at the pre-registered sampling temperature estimates the seed component and the SD of the paired success difference (0.7 assumed, 0.95 conservative) before any cell is sized. B bank construction: 400 held-out train games at k=0 with one self-written reflection per game, kept regardless of outcome (about 200 usable items of visibly varying quality), 400 episodes; these games are excluded from every later cell. E1 main LOO cell: 1,200 train-stream games x 2 seeds x k=3, base plus 3 single-item removals = 9,600 episodes (about 8 h on two replicas). Bank = expert items + self-written items + 100 planted wrong-procedure items (expert items with one procedural step replaced by a wrong action for the type) + 20 scene-matched solution items (expert trajectory of a same-scene same-type game, so object locations match). Forcing: each planted wrong-procedure item is forced into position 2 or 3 of 10 randomly chosen episodes (1,000 forced episodes, 10 retrievals each); each scene-matched item into the 12 episodes (6 games x 2 seeds) of its scene cluster (240); the remaining 1,160 episodes use the natural retriever set. The 1,200 games are chosen from the 3,553 train games in a free offline retrieval pass, stratified by task type, so that a panel of 120 natural items (>= 80 expert, >= 40 self-written) each receive >= 24 retrievals (>= 12 games x 2 seeds), split into game-disjoint halves A and B with >= 12 retrievals each. Per (item, game, seed): delta = y(S) - y(S minus i), y the success flag. E2 REPLACE ground truth: 150 stream games x 2 seeds x 3 token-matched cross-type replacements = 900 episodes (base from E1); class-level REMOVE vs REPLACE agreement within 5 net (planted, expert, self-written classes) is a pre-registered validity check, panel Spearman reported. Arms: S6 and S24 (bottom 100 by LOO mean from E1 retrievals subsampled to n = 6 and n = 24 per item; items with fewer use all they have), R (random 100, fresh draw per game), O (oracle: the 100 planted). Name: utility_half_life_consumer_swap
Title: Harm Travels, Help Does Not: Re-measuring Learned Memory Utilities Against Replace-Static Intervention Value After Reader Swap, Store Growth and Layout Shift
Short Hypothesis: A learned per-item utility is a statement about one reader, one store and one query distribution. After the reader is swapped, the store grows with self-written items, or the layouts change from seen to unseen, the intervention-measured value of helpful expert items is lost (retained value falls by at least 10 net beyond what a same-reader re-measurement loses, or by at least 5 net relative to the unchanged store) while the value of wrong-procedure items persists (at most -10 net in every condition), so the learned utility keeps its power to flag harm and loses its power to rank help; and re-validating it by a short intervention costs fewer episodes than re-learning it from the stream under the new reader, judged against a criterion independent of both routes. Contribution in one sentence: intervention-measured transfer asymmetry of item value across three drift arms, each with a same-reader replication or composition control that nets out re-measurement noise, plus the cost curve of re-validation versus re-learning against an independent criterion.
Related Work: ExpSuite (arXiv:2605.30712) claims executor-agnostic experience reuse but does not isolate whether utilities learned under one executor hold under another; MemQ (arXiv:2605.08374) and MERIT (arXiv:2606.00547) learn values on a fixed stream and do not re-measure them; ReMe (arXiv:2512.10696) reports a memory-scaling effect without item-level transfer; the freshness-weighted memory (s2:eddd4453) and SF-AMS (arXiv:2607.22562) decay by time, not by measured value change; Memora (arXiv:2604.20006) and MINTEval (arXiv:2605.18565) show reuse of invalidated memories at the outcome level only; the continual-learning view (arXiv:2604.27003) relocates stability-plasticity to retrieval without item attribution; the compliance trap (arXiv:2607.10608) shows wrong memory harms stronger agents more, which motivates the harm-transfers half of the hypothesis and supplies its reverse outcome (a weaker second reader harmed less). In the home literature, training-data attribution is evaluated by the linear datamodeling score (arXiv:2410.13850) and representation methods (AirRep arXiv:2505.18513) aim at model-aligned attributions, but transfer of attribution scores across consumer models is not reported for stored items. The archived idea memory_item_value_reliability (6.12) asserted that item value is not an item property; it had no intervention arm and effects under the noise floor. This proposal supplies the intervention under each condition with its own control arm, sizes classes to +/-4.5 net (+/-3.2 in the natural-composition cells), nets out re-measurement noise with a same-reader replication, and makes an asymmetric prediction that can come out reversed.
Abstract: Learned memory utilities are trained once and trusted thereafter. We ask what they are still worth after three ordinary changes: the reader model is swapped, the store grows, and the query distribution shifts. On ALFWorld we learn per-item outcome Q over the 3,553-game train stream with Qwen3-32B and the expert bank, then measure forced-retrieval, token-matched replace-static value for three item classes (40 each: expert procedural, planted wrong-procedure, and location-specific 'stale-true' items whose receptacle claim holds in seen layouts only) under a reference condition and three drift arms on the same games: reader swap to a second local backbone chosen by a pre-registered rule from a closed two-candidate list; store growth by 1,892 self-written items, measured in the grown store's natural retrieval set; and layout shift to valid_unseen. Each drift arm carries its own control that nets out re-measurement noise: a same-reader replication on an independent seed family for the swap, a one-item composition swap in the unchanged store for growth, and a location-clause-edited copy of each item for the layout shift. We report, per class and condition, the retained value, the loss of value relative to the control, the rank correlation of the reference-trained Q with each condition's ground truth, and the episodes an intervention needs to re-rank a class against an independent criterion versus the stream games a Q re-learned under the new reader needs. Predictions: helpful expert items lose at least 10 net of retained value under the swap while wrong-procedure items lose at most 4 net and stay at or below -10 net; expert items are worth at least 5 net less in the grown store than in the expert store with or without one self-written neighbour; location-specific items are at least +10 net on seen and at most -10 net on unseen layouts and editing out the location clause restores at least 10 net; the pooled correlation of the reference Q with ground truth drops by at least 0.20 under swap and under shift; and a 16-pair intervention re-ranks the class at Spearman 0.5 against the independent criterion while the re-learned Q is below 0.25 at 2,000 stream games. About 38 GPU-pair hours with both GPUs busy throughout.
Experiments:
- Ground-truth protocol (all cells): forced-retrieval intervention paired on (game, sampling seed). For item i of class C, 24 same-type evaluation games x 2 sampling seeds = 48 pairs (96 pairs = 24 games x 4 seeds in the three natural-composition EP cells). Arms per pair: WITH (i in the k=3 set) and REPLACE-static (i replaced by the type's static procedure sentence padded to i's token count; Measurement C baseline, so the primary estimand is item value net of the static prompt); REMOVE (k=2 set) only in the additivity probe. Two compositions: THIN = i at rank 1 plus the two natural cross-type retrievals as fillers, so i carries the set (chosen because in the natural k=3 set the measured +17.2-net residual over static3 is shared by three items, leaving about 4-6 net per item, below per-item noise); NATURAL = i plus the natural same-type top-2 of the store in force. Seed families: F1 = {s1,s2}, F2 = {s3,s4}, F3 = {s5,s6}. Per-item SE about 10 net at 48 pairs (7 net at 96); a 40-item cell = 1,920 pairs gives a class CI of about +/-4.5 net (3,840 pairs: +/-3.2); paired differences between two cells on the same items, games and seeds have CI about +/-5 (48 pairs) and +/-4 (96 pairs). Throughput 20 episodes/min per replica, 40/min on both GPUs: a 40-item 2-arm 48-pair cell = 3,840 episodes = 1.6 h; a 2-arm 96-pair cell = 7,680 episodes = 3.2 h.
- E0 Reader pilot and gates (0.5 h, one candidate per GPU): closed pre-registered candidate list in order: (1) Qwen3-14B, (2) Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Both are run on all 274 evaluation games (140 valid_seen + 134 valid_unseen) x 1 seed at k=0, static3 and k=3 (822 episodes each) and both are reported in full. Selection rule, fixed before any E2 cell: the first candidate in list order whose k=0 success on valid_seen lies in [0.30, 0.70] and whose k3 - k0 gain is >= +10 net. If neither passes, the B arm becomes a decoding-regime swap of the reference reader (thinking on versus off), pre-registered as the fallback and labelled the weaker manipulation in every table; there is no search beyond the two candidates. The chosen reader's k3 - static3 residual is reported as a moderator next to P1, whose sharp form is that a reader which demonstrably profits from the bank does not profit from the same items.
- E1 Learning pass (3 h per stream on one GPU; two streams in parallel, one per GPU): per-item outcome Q (count-average and EMA alpha=0.1) from one pass over the 3,553-game train stream under the reference reader with the expert bank and natural k=3 retrieval; MemQ-style TD(lambda) on the same log as a second scorer; feedback counts recorded. Second stream seed for test-retest. A mixed-stream variant refits the same Q on the union of the seed-1 log and the E4 unseen-game log, so that its LS rank is not fixed by seen-only training.
- E2 Ground-truth cells (33.2 h; hours per cell): classes EP (40 expert procedural items with positive nested-k position value in the existing logs), W (40 planted wrong-procedure items), LS (40 location-specific expert items whose receptacle claim holds in the seen layout; regex plus manual check). (a) R1: reference reader, expert bank, valid_seen, THIN, F1, 2 arms; EP, W, LS: 4.8 h. (b) R2: as R1 with F2, classes EP and W: 3.2 h (same-reader replication; the baseline for P1). (c) B: second reader, expert bank, valid_seen, THIN, F2, 2 arms; EP, W, LS: 4.8 h. (d) U: reference reader, expert bank, valid_unseen type-matched games, THIN, F1, 2 arms; EP, W, LS: 4.8 h. (e) U-edit: the 40 LS items with the location clause removed (token-matched), U as in (d): 1.6 h. (f) R-nat: reference reader, expert bank, valid_seen, NATURAL (expert store's same-type top-2), 96 pairs (F1 u F2), 2 arms, EP: 3.2 h. (g) R-swap: as (f) but the natural top-1 replaced by the highest-similarity self-pool item (one-item composition change, store unchanged), EP, 96 pairs: 3.2 h. (h) G: reference reader, store = expert bank + 1,892 self-pool items, NATURAL from the grown store (its own top-2, which may be self-written; the fraction of sets containing a self-written item is reported and, if below 0.5, the cell is re-run once with the self-written top-1 forced in, pre-registered), valid_seen, EP, 96 pairs, 2 arms: 3.2 h. (i) Composition replicates: 20-item subsamples of W and of LS re-measured under NATURAL in R (F1, 2 arms): 1.6 h. (j) Criterion K for P5: second reader, NATURAL (expert store), F3, EP, 2 arms, 48 pairs: 1.6 h. (k) Additivity probe: 20 EP items in R-nat with arms REMOVE-i, REMOVE-j (natural top-1) and REMOVE-ij, 48 pairs: 1.2 h.
- E3 Re-validation cost (stream 1.5 GPU-pair h; analysis free): (i) intervention route: the B THIN F2 pairs subsampled at 4, 8, 16, 24, 48 per item; (ii) re-learning route: the 3,553-game train stream under the second reader (3 h on GPU 1), Q_B fitted on prefixes of 500, 1,000, 2,000 and 3,553 games. Both routes are scored by Spearman with the independent criterion K (cell j: different composition and different seed family from route (i); K is measured under the natural-retrieval regime that route (ii) learns from, so it favours the stream route if anything). K's split-half reliability (s5 vs s6) is the ceiling drawn on both curves. Episodes are counted in total for both routes; no zero-marginal accounting.
- E4 Lag of the learned rule (0.1 h): the reference Q continues online through the 134 unseen games x 2 seeds under natural retrieval; for LS items the retrievals until Q (count-average and EMA) crosses below the store median are recorded and set against the intervention pairs needed to detect the LS class sign at -10 net (40 x 16 pairs = 640 pairs, CI +/-7.8). Reported as an estimand; no numeric prediction.
- Budget: E0 0.5 + E1 3.0 (two 3-h streams, one per GPU) + E2 33.2 + E3(ii) 1.5 + E4 0.1 = about 38 GPU-pair hours, about two days wall-clock with both GPUs busy: the second reader serves on GPU 1 for cells (c), (j) and E3(ii) while GPU 0 serves cells (d)-(i) and E1; nohup, pid files, resumable append-only JSONL; gates, selection rules and thresholds pre-registered before any E2 cell. Cut to pay for the new arms: the self-written class as a measured class (self-written items now enter only as the grown store's co-retrieved items), the REMOVE arm outside the additivity probe, and store-growth cells for W and LS.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Scorers: per-item outcome Q (count-average, EMA alpha=0.1), MemQ-style TD(lambda), usage-count control, similarity-only control, the mixed-stream Q variant; Q_B re-learned under the second reader for E3.
- Ground truth: REPLACE-static (item value net of the type's static procedure sentence) in every cell as the primary estimand; REMOVE in the additivity probe; the nested-k position contrast from the existing logs as the free reference used only to pick the EP class.
- Composition as a manipulated variable: THIN and NATURAL for the EP class in R (cells a, f), a one-item swap control (g) and the grown store (h); 20-item NATURAL replicates of W and LS (i) so every class is reported under two compositions; the additivity probe (k) tests pairwise versus single removal on 20 EP items with their natural top-1 (interaction = value(REMOVE-ij) - value(REMOVE-i) - value(REMOVE-j)), reported with its CI and not assumed zero.
- Same-reader replication (b) on an independent seed family as the loss and flip baseline for P1.
- Class ablation: LS items with the location clause edited out under U (e), the mechanism conjunct of P3.
- Controls kept from the prior round: same pool and bank-target partition in all conditions; token-matched placebos; k=0 and static3 arms per reader as floors; the aggregate k3 - static3 residual (+17.2 net at the natural bank) re-reported per reader and condition as a sanity check.
Falsifiable Predictions:

Selection: items with |REPLACE-static value| >= 10 net in R1 (THIN, F1); counts per class reported (pre-registered fallback: if fewer than 20 EP items pass, the cutoff drops to 7 net and is reported with the resulting CI). Retained value v' = sign(R1) x value. Same-reader loss L_RR,C = mean over selected items of [v'(R1) - v'(R2)] measures the selection's regression to the mean and is reported; swap loss L_C = mean over selected items of [v'(R2) - v'(B)], paired on item and game with seed family F2 in both cells, so neither term was used for selection and regression to the mean is excluded by construction. Prediction: L_EP >= 10 net and L_W <= 4 net, and the W class mean under B (all 40 items) is <= -10 net. Falsified if L_EP <= 3 net (help transfers), or L_W >= 10 net, or the W class mean under B is >= -5 net (harm does not transfer). Noise: about 25 selected EP items with per-item paired SE 14 net give CI about +/-5.5 on L_EP, so 10 versus 3 is resolvable; L_W over about 35 items has CI +/-4.6 (4 versus 10 resolvable); the W-under-B cell has CI +/-4.5 (-10 versus -5 at the edge, reported with its CI). The excess sign-flip rate f_RB - f_RR per class is reported with 1,000-item bootstrap CIs at 5, 10 and 15 net cutoffs as the descriptive companion, not as the test. Arms: E2 (a), (b), (c); moderator: the chosen reader's k3 - static3 residual from E0. Not entailed: the compliance-trap result predicts a weaker second reader is harmed less by wrong items (L_W large, W under B near zero), and a reader that follows expert procedures as the reference does gives L_EP near zero; both are reachable under cell (c).
- P2 Store-growth substitution (NATURAL, EP, 96 pairs). Gate (pre-registered): EP class mean REPLACE-static in R-nat >= +6 net (CI +/-3.2); if it fails P2 is void and reported as a failed positive control (expert items have no measurable individual value beside two expert neighbours, itself a within-expert-store substitution result quantified by the additivity probe). Prediction: G - R-nat <= -5 net and G - R-swap <= -5 net on the same items, games and seeds, i.e. the item is worth at least 5 net less in the grown store's natural set than in the expert store's set both without and with one self-written neighbour, so the drop is carried by the grown store and not by a self-written neighbour as such. Falsified if G - R-nat >= 0 net (no collapse) or G - R-swap >= 0 net (the one-item swap already produces the drop: a composition effect, not a store effect). Paired-difference CI about +/-4 net at 96 pairs, so -5 versus 0 is resolvable. Arms: E2 (f), (g), (h). Not entailed: the grown store's top-2 may remain expert items, or self-written neighbours may be worse substitutes and raise the item's value.
- P3 Stale-true items flip sign across layouts (THIN). Prediction: LS class mean REPLACE-static >= +10 net in R1 and <= -10 net in U, and the location clause carries the flip: U-edit - U >= +10 net on the same games and seeds. Falsified if the U effect is >= -2 net (the reader does not act on a wrong location claim), or R1 - U < 8 net, or U-edit - U <= +3 net (the flip is carried by the rest of the item). Noise: each cell CI +/-4.5; R1 - U on different game sets CI about +/-6.4; U-edit - U paired CI about +/-5; the gaps (12, 12 and 7 net) exceed the corresponding CIs. The seen-only Q rank of LS items is reported but not predicted (it is fixed by seen-only training); the mixed-stream Q's rank of the LS class median and the E4 lag are reported as estimands. Arms: E2 (a), (d), (e); E1 mixed-stream fit; E4.

Gate (pre-registered, separate from the falsifier): Spearman(reference Q, R1 REPLACE-static ground truth) pooled over EP, W, LS (120 items) >= 0.30, else P4 is void and reported as a failed positive control. Prediction: the pooled Spearman falls by >= 0.20 from R1 to B and from R1 to U (raw and disattenuated by split-seed reliability: s1 vs s2 for R1 and U, s3 vs s4 for B), and each drop exceeds the test-retest gap between the two E1 stream seeds' Qs by >= 0.10. Falsified if the drop is < 0.10 in both B and U, or does not exceed the test-retest gap. Secondary: within-class Spearman on EP alone, to show the drop is not only the W-versus-rest contrast that P1 predicts stays. Noise: bootstrap over the same 120 items of the difference of two Spearmans (SE about 0.06), so 0.20 versus 0.10 is resolvable. Arms: E2 (a), (c), (d) scored by E1. Shared term with P1: W values transferring floors the pooled drop; that is why the falsifier sits at 0.10 and the EP-only correlation is reported.
- P5 Re-validation cost against an independent criterion. Criterion K: B-condition EP values under NATURAL composition and seed family F3 (cell j), independent of route (i) in both composition and seeds, and measured under the retrieval regime route (ii) learns from; K's split-half reliability (s5 vs s6) is the ceiling shown on both curves. Prediction: the intervention route (B THIN F2 subsampled) reaches Spearman >= 0.5 with K at <= 16 pairs per item (<= 16 x 2 arms x 40 = 1,280 episodes), while the re-learned Q_B is <= 0.25 at 2,000 stream games (2,000 episodes) and does not reach 0.5 by 3,553. Falsified if Q_B reaches 0.5 by 1,000 games, or the intervention route is <= 0.25 at 48 pairs (thin-composition values do not predict natural-composition values under the new reader, so the cheap probe cannot re-validate either). Noise: Spearman over 40 items has SE about 0.12 at rho 0.5, so 0.5 versus 0.25 is two SE; bootstrap over items. Episodes counted in total for both routes. Arms: E3 (i), (ii); E2 (j).
- Gates (pre-registered pass/fail preconditions, not hypothesis tests; each has a reachable failing outcome and a stated consequence): G1 second reader from the closed two-candidate list under the E0 rule, both candidates reported, fallback = decoding-regime swap; G2 harm class manufacturable: W class mean REPLACE-static in R1 <= -10 net (CI +/-4.5), else the W class is re-planted with stronger wrong procedures once and, failing that, the harm half of P1 is reported as unmanufacturable; G3 the P2 natural-composition gate (>= +6 net); G4 the P4 R1 correlation gate (>= 0.30).

Name: guilt_by_coretrieval
Title: Guilt by Co-retrieval: Measuring Reward Contamination of Learned Memory Utilities Against Leave-One-Out Ground Truth
Short Hypothesis: When an outcome reward is shared by all co-retrieved memory items, the learned utility of an innocent item is pulled toward the counterfactual value of whatever it is co-retrieved with (RoMeRL's memory-reward trap). We claim this contamination is a dose-response quantity that scrambles the ranking of items by their true intervention value: if the fraction of an item's retrievals that co-occur with a planted wrong-procedure item is randomised across items (dose 0, 0.5, 1), the rank correlation between learned per-item Q and leave-one-out (LOO) ground truth falls by at least the pre-registered minimum detectable effect (0.20 at n=120) although the items' own LOO value is unchanged; provenance-DAG credit (MemQ) and reduced-order utility coordinates (RoMeRL) recover at most a quarter of that loss because both still pool siblings retrieved for the same task, whereas a scorer that de-pools (flag-oracle, or LOO-corrected Q on a 20% subsample of stream episodes) recovers most of it, at a measured LLM-call cost. Contribution: the first measurement of learned per-item memory utilities against intervention ground truth under manipulated co-retrieval, giving the contamination slope, the failure of two published remedies against a reachable upper bound, and a costed fix.
Related Work: RoMeRL (arXiv:2608.02508) names the memory-reward trap and argues that fixed-dimensional per-task utility states limit contamination, but validates only downstream success, never an item's leave-one-out (LOO) effect. MemQ (arXiv:2605.08374) propagates TD(lambda) credit over a provenance DAG; siblings at one DAG level still share the outcome. REMEMBERER (arXiv:2306.07929) and MemRL (arXiv:2601.03192) update every retrieved experience toward the episode return. Memory-R2 (arXiv:2605.21768) and CHIME (arXiv:2609.02074) describe fair or credit-aware assignment for training or write-time policies but report no counterfactual check on stored items. UCOB (arXiv:2606.29502) and ExpSuite (arXiv:2605.30712) compare with-set versus without-set, which cannot split credit inside the set. On the ground-truth side, CUE-R (arXiv:2604.05467) and document Shapley (arXiv:2507.04480) measure per-item intervention effects for single-shot RAG only; Data Shapley (arXiv:1904.02868) is the home-literature ancestor of LOO valuation and reports that noisy per-datum values need many retraining samples, which is why our class is sized to a pre-registered MDE. None of these manipulates co-retrieval as a dose or scores a learned utility by its rank correlation with LOO.
Abstract: Self-evolving memory systems attach a learned utility to every stored item, but the utility is learned from a reward the whole retrieved set shares, so an item's score reflects its neighbours. We measure this contamination directly on the ALFWorld expert bank with a Qwen3-32B reader. A class B of 120 bystander expert items (stratified across terciles of the free nested-k position-contrast estimate so that within-class value varies) each receives 24 scheduled stream episodes of its task type with the item forced at rank 3; the rank-2 slot is always replaced (constant churn), by a planted wrong-procedure item W with probability d and by a random same-type expert item otherwise. In two mixed passes each B item is randomly assigned d in {0, 0.5, 1} (40 items per dose, rotated between passes); two all-dose-0 passes with different seeds give the reference and the test-retest floor. Four scorer families are fit offline on each pass: per-item outcome Q (REMEMBERER-style), TD(lambda) over a provenance DAG (MemQ-style), reduced-order per-task coordinates (RoMeRL-style), and two de-pooling scorers: a flag-oracle Q that ignores W-containing episodes (zero cost, reachable upper bound) and an LOO-corrected Q that re-runs REMOVE per retrieved item on a 10/20/40/100% subsample of scheduled episodes and updates only items whose removal flips the outcome. Ground truth is forced-retrieval WITH versus token-matched REPLACE-static3 on the same (game, seed), 48 pairs per item, under a clean composition (all 120 items) and a W-containing composition (48 items), with REMOVE (k=2) on 40 items to report the static-versus-removal gap. Scorers are scored by Spearman with LOO, raw and disattenuated by split-seed reliability, with item-level bootstrap CIs and a pre-registered MDE of 0.20 for the dose contrast. Additivity is tested at class level on 40 helpful+conflicting and 40 helpful+redundant four-arm sets (CI about +/-5 net). Predictions: the mixed-dose Spearman falls by >= 0.20 relative to the dose-0 pass; MemQ and RoMeRL recover <= 25% of that loss while the flag-oracle recovers >= 75%; the 20%-subsample corrected Q comes within 0.05 of the dose-0 correlation and its measured cost is reported; class-mean interaction is <= -10 net in both manufactured set kinds; dose-1 items make up >= 60% of the pruned bottom quartile. About 49,500 episodes, 41 h on two A100s with one vLLM replica per GPU.
Experiments:
- Ground-truth protocol (all cells): forced-retrieval intervention on the same (game, seed). Item i is forced into the k=3 set at rank 3 with the natural top-2 (composition i) or with a same-type W item at rank 2 (composition ii); 24 same-type evaluation games x 2 seeds = 48 pairs. Arms: WITH (i present) and REPLACE-static3 (i replaced by the type's static3 exemplar sentence padded to i's token count; Measurement C baseline, so per-item value is net of the static prompt by construction). Per-item value = mean paired success difference (SE ~0.10 at p=0.5); a 120-item class gives a class CI of about +/-2.6 net, 40 items about +/-4.5 net. Cost per item = 96 episodes; throughput 20 episodes/min on two replicas.
- Stream passes (E1; 673 unscheduled stream games run once = 0.6 h, plus 2,880 scheduled episodes per pass = 2.4 h): bank frozen (expert bank; W items enter only through the manipulation). Pass A: all B at dose 0. Pass A': dose 0, second stream and sampler seed (test-retest). Pass M1: dose randomised per item, 40/40/40 across {0, 0.5, 1}, stratified by tercile and task type. Pass M2: assignment rotated so each item gets a different dose than in M1. The rank-2 slot is replaced in every scheduled episode (W with probability d, else random same-type expert item), so dose changes wrongness only, not set size or churn. Logged per episode: retrieved ids, ranks, outcome, planted flag. Scorers fit offline per pass: per-item Q (count-average and alpha=0.1); MemQ TD(lambda in {0.5, 0.9}) over the retrieval DAG; RoMeRL-style per-task-type state (dim 4/16/64) updated by outcome, item utility = projection of the item embedding onto the state; usage-count and similarity-only controls; flag-oracle Q (B updated only from episodes without a W item). 4 x 2.4 + 0.6 = 10.2 h.
- Corrected-Q re-runs (on M1 scheduled episodes only, the episodes in which B items are updated): one REMOVE re-run per retrieved item (3 per episode) on a nested 10/20/40% subsample of all 120 items' scheduled episodes (3,456 episodes) and a 100% ceiling on a 40-item stratified subset (1,728 extra episodes); update rule: an item receives the outcome only if its removal flips success. 5,184 episodes = 4.3 h. Cost is measured (episodes, prompt and generated tokens per stream episode), not asserted.
- E0 Positive controls, run first. (a) W class (40 planted items, one per task type x layout, each swapping the target receptacle or omitting the clean/heat/cool step): clean-composition value <= -10 net, else contamination cannot be manufactured and the study stops (3,840 episodes, 3.2 h). (b) Scorer-validity gate within the B class alone: after the first 60 B items are ground-truthed, Spearman(pass-A per-item Q, LOO) over those 60 items >= 0.25 (SE ~0.12) and the A-vs-A' test-retest Spearman of Q vectors >= 0.5; W items are excluded from the gate so between-class separation cannot carry it.
- E2 Ground truth: composition (i) for all 120 B items (11,520 episodes, 9.6 h); composition (ii) for a 48-item stratified subset (4,608 episodes, 3.8 h); REMOVE (k=2) arm on 40 B items (1,920 episodes, 1.6 h) to report REMOVE minus REPLACE-static3. Report per-item and class values, split-seed reliability, Spearman(scorer, LOO) per pass with 1,000 item-level bootstraps, raw and disattenuated; the class-mean B value is stated against the measured k3 - static3 residual of +17.2 net.
- E3 Additivity, class level: 40 helpful+conflicting sets (B, W at ranks 2-3 with the natural rank-1) and 40 helpful+redundant sets (B, B' same type and procedure), each on 16 games x 2 seeds = 32 pairs, four arms (full, -B, -W or -B', -both). Interaction I = s_full - s_-B - s_-W + s_-both per set (per-set SE ~15 net), averaged per kind (SE ~2.4 net, CI about +/-5). 10,240 episodes, 8.5 h.
- E4 Decision cost: bottom-quartile (30 items) of each pass's Q vector crossed with clean LOO; dose composition of the pruned quartile; extra episodes and tokens per stream episode for corrected Q at each subsample rate versus the 100% ceiling.
- Budget: 673 + 11,520 + 5,184 + 3,840 + 11,520 + 4,608 + 1,920 + 10,240 = 49,505 episodes = 41.3 h at 20 episodes/min on two A100s, one vLLM replica per GPU, workers tuned to keep each replica's running queue >= 8; ground-truth cells run on one replica while the next pass runs on the other; nohup, pid files, resumable JSONL. Thresholds and the MDE are pre-registered before pass M1; if a 32-h cap is imposed, E3 drops to 30+30 sets and E2(ii) to 36 items, nothing else moves.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Scorer baselines (one per family): per-item outcome Q (REMEMBERER/MemRL style); MemQ-style TD(lambda) over the retrieval DAG; RoMeRL-style reduced-order coordinates; usage-count (no-outcome control); similarity-only rank (no-learning control); flag-oracle Q (reachable upper bound that de-pools with perfect information); LOO-corrected Q at 10/20/40/100% subsample (costed de-pooling).
- Ground-truth baselines: REPLACE-static3 (primary, Measurement C) versus REMOVE k=2 on 40 items; nested-k position contrast from runs/sweep/k_sweep_final.jsonl as the free position-level estimate and as the stratification variable for the B class.
- Composition: every per-item estimate reported under the clean and the W-containing composition on the 48-item subset; additivity tested in E3 at class level.
- Learning-rule ablations (offline, free): count-average versus alpha=0.1 Q; MemQ lambda in {0.5, 0.9}; RoMeRL state dimension {4, 16, 64}; corrected-Q subsample rate 10/20/40/100%; flip-only versus difference-weighted update.
- Placebo: the rank-2 slot is replaced in every scheduled episode, W or random same-type expert item, token-matched to the displaced item, so dose 0 has identical churn to dose 1.
- Test-retest: pass A' repeats pass A with a second seed; the A-vs-A' difference in Spearman(Q, LOO) is the noise floor every dose effect must clear.
- Removed: the self-written-item control (carried no prediction; cut to fit the envelope).
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (headline) Contamination scrambles ranks: Spearman(per-item Q, clean LOO) over the 120 B items is lower in the mixed-dose passes (mean of M1 and M2) than in pass A by >= 0.20, the pre-registered MDE (analytic SE of a dependent-correlation difference at n=120 is ~0.08, giving 80% power at 0.20; the empirical A-vs-A' SE replaces the analytic one before M1 is scored and, if larger, the MDE is raised and stated). Falsified if the drop is < 0.10 with the item-bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0.20, or if the drop does not exceed the A-vs-A' test-retest difference. Arm: passes M1/M2 versus A, scored against E2(i). Not entailed: a shift common to all items of a dose group only reorders ranks if it exceeds the between-item spread of true value; if B items override the planted W at rank 2 (E2(ii) shows B's W-composition value close to its clean value) the W episodes carry no contamination and the correlation holds. The class-mean drop in B's Q with dose is reported only as a manipulation check, since it follows from E0(a).
- P2 Published remedies do not de-pool: on the mixed passes, MemQ TD(lambda) and RoMeRL coordinates each recover <= 25% of the P1 drop (their Spearman with LOO is within 0.05 of per-item Q), while the flag-oracle Q recovers >= 75%. Falsified if either remedy recovers >= 75% of the drop (Spearman >= per-item Q + 0.15) with CI excluding 25%; void (reported as such) if the flag-oracle itself recovers < 50%, which would mean the loss is not from pooling. Reachable mechanism for the falsifier: RoMeRL's projection can separate W from B if their embeddings load on different state directions, and MemQ with lambda=0.5 discounts multi-hop credit; both are run at three settings.
- P3 Costed fix, absolute: on M1, Spearman(corrected Q at 20% subsample, LOO) >= Spearman(Q, LOO on pass A) - 0.05 and >= Spearman(Q, LOO on M1) + 0.10, with recovery monotone in subsample rate. Falsified if the 20% scorer is <= per-item Q + 0.05 with CI excluding +0.10 while the 100% ceiling reaches pass-A level (the subsample is insufficient), or if the 100% ceiling itself stays below pass-A level - 0.10 (the estimator does not work at any cost). Cost is an estimand: measured extra episodes and tokens per stream episode at each rate, compared with a full LOO pass.
- P4 Non-additivity at class level: the class-mean interaction I is <= -10 net in helpful+conflicting sets and <= -10 net in helpful+redundant sets (single removals over-count), each with a 95% CI excluding 0; in redundant sets the mean single-removal effects are each > -5 net while the pair removal is <= -10 net. Falsified if the class-mean I is > -5 net with CI excluding -10 in either kind (additivity holds, so single-removal LOO is a fair estimator). Arm: E3, 40 sets per kind, SE ~2.4 net.
- P5 Decision consequence: in the mixed passes, dose-1 items make up >= 60% of the pruned bottom quartile (18 or more of 30; 10 expected under no contamination, binomial SE ~2.6), and the false-prune rate (bottom-quartile items with clean LOO >= +5 net) is >= 2x its pass-A rate, evaluated only if the pass-A rate lies in the pre-registered window [0.10, 0.45] where a 2x ratio is attainable. Falsified if dose-1 items are <= 13 of 30 in both mixed passes, or the rate ratio is < 1.3 with the paired-bootstrap CI excluding 2. Arm: E4 on passes A, M1, M2.
- P6 Gates (must pass before M1 is scored): E0(a) W-class clean value <= -10 net (CI +/-4.5); E0(b) within-B Spearman(pass-A Q, LOO) >= 0.25 over the first 60 ground-truthed B items and A-vs-A' Q test-retest >= 0.5. Either failure stops the confirmatory cells; the result is reported as a failed manipulation or an invalid scorer, not as a finding. The within-B gate can fail if the stratified B class has too little true spread or the reader ignores rank-3 items.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired design throughout: every intervention arm re-runs the same (game, seed) with the retrieved set changed only at the manipulated slot; env and sampler seeded per episode. Per-item LOO reliability is estimated by split-seed halves (Spearman-Brown corrected) and used to disattenuate scorer correlations; raw and corrected values are reported. Per-item Q is an average over 24 scheduled outcomes (SE ~0.10), matched to the LOO per-item SE; class cells: 120 items (~+/-2.6 net), 40-item subsets (~+/-4.5 net). The dose contrast is between-item within a pass and within-item across the two rotated mixed passes; correlation differences use 1,000 item-level bootstraps. Pre-registered MDE for P1: 0.20 at n=120, or the empirical A-vs-A' SE x 2.5 if larger. Test-retest of the learning pass (A vs A') is reported for every scorer; a dose effect must exceed it. Cost estimands: pairs per item to reach split-half LOO reliability 0.5, extra episodes and tokens per stream episode for corrected Q at each rate. Both GPUs stay busy by running E2 cells on one replica while the next pass runs on the other; throughput (episodes/min, tok/s per GPU) and queue depth are logged with each status update.
