Name: admission_pruning_audit_random_holdout
Title: Admit Everything Once: Auditing Write-Time Utility Scores and Outcome-Based Pruning Against Realized Counterfactual Item Value
Short Hypothesis: Write-time admission scores (A-MAC-style factor admission, RPE-critic surprise/utility, DIG-style confidence gain) do not predict the realized counterfactual value of a memory item beyond rank correlation 0.2, so bypassed items are as valuable as admitted ones; and outcome-based pruning beats random pruning only for items that have accumulated at least 8 feedback events, a threshold fewer than one store item in five reaches in a 3,553-game stream, so most pruning decisions in a self-evolving store are made at random-equivalent precision. Contribution in one sentence: a randomized-holdout audit that puts admission and pruning error rates, and the feedback count a pruning decision needs, on an intervention scale.
Related Work: A-MAC (arXiv:2603.04549) admits by five interpretable factors and reports precision-recall against annotated relevance, not realized utility; the RPE-critic router (arXiv:2603.14597) gates writes by surprise and predicted utility and reports cost, not the fate of bypassed items; SF-AMS (arXiv:2607.22562) and Oblivion (arXiv:2604.00131) prune or decay by usage-derived utility and validate by aggregate accuracy only; ReMe (arXiv:2512.10696) utility-refines but does not report pruning errors; DIG (arXiv:2509.12765) scores documents by confidence gain one at a time in single-shot RAG. Memory Reward Inflation (arXiv:2608.00017) shows self-graded rewards inflate wrong episodes in text-to-SQL and proposes answer-free de-inflation; our rewards are environment-verified, so any entrenchment we find is not grading inflation. Utility-driven replay (s2:05c14833) evicts by reward magnitude and TD error on classic control. In data valuation, Data Shapley (arXiv:1904.02868) and DVGS (arXiv:2405.08217) rank data for removal but validate by retrain curves, the analogue of our forced-retrieval LOO; no memory system has run that curve for its admission or pruning rule. The archived idea utility_pruning_is_frequency_pruning was rejected as entailed by the pruning rule; this proposal audits outcomes, not the rule.
Abstract: Every self-evolving memory decides twice about an item: whether to admit it and whether to keep it. Both decisions are made from scores whose relation to the item's realized effect has never been measured, because a bypassed item is never seen again. We run a randomized-holdout audit on ALFWorld with a Qwen3-32B reader. All 1,892 self-pool successes plus 40 planted wrong-procedure items enter a shadow store regardless of any rule; three write-time scorers (A-MAC-style factors, RPE-critic surprise/utility, DIG-style confidence gain on one held-out same-type game) score every candidate. A stratified sample of 160 candidates spanning each scorer's quartiles is then evaluated by forced-retrieval ADD (item forced into the k=3 set versus token-matched static-procedure placebo) on 24 games x 2 seeds each, giving realized value on the same (game, seed). After one pass of the train stream with per-item outcome Q feeding retrieval, and a second pass with usage-decay (SF-AMS-style) utility feeding retrieval, we prune the bottom 20% by each score and a random 20%, and measure the pruned items' realized value stratified by feedback count (1-3, 4-7, >= 8). We report admission rank correlation with realized value, false-bypass cost (realized value of bypassed items), harmless-prune and harmful-item-capture rates versus random, the feedback count at which outcome pruning beats random, the fraction of store items reaching it, and the retrieval share of planted wrong items across stream thirds under the two utility rules. Predictions: no write-time scorer exceeds rank correlation 0.2 with realized value; admitted and bypassed items differ by less than 5 net; outcome-Q pruning beats random by >= 0.15 in harmful-item capture only at >= 8 feedback events; under usage-decay utility the wrong items' retrieval share rises across the stream. About 20 GPU-pair hours.
Experiments:
- Ground-truth protocol (shared by all cells): forced-retrieval intervention on the same (game, seed). For a sampled item i of class C, take 24 same-type evaluation games x 2 seeds = 48 paired episodes with i forced into the k=3 set at rank 3 (the other two slots are the natural top-2 retrievals, or a manipulated composition). Arms per pair: WITH (i present), ADD/REMOVE (item absent, k=2 set), REPLACE-static (i replaced by the type's static procedure sentence padded to i's token count; Measurement C baseline, so REPLACE-static is item value net of the static prompt). Per-item effect = mean paired success difference; per-item SE about 0.10 at p=0.5; a 40-item class = 1,920 pairs gives a class CI of about +/-4.5 net. Cost per class per condition: 40 items x 48 pairs x 2 extra arms = 3,840 episodes = 3.2 h at 20 episodes/min on two replicas.
- E0 Positive control, cheapest first (~3.5 h): 40 expert procedural items versus 40 planted wrong-procedure items under forced-retrieval ADD must separate by >= 15 net; otherwise the audit lacks power and stops.
- E1 Admission audit (~6.4 h of re-runs plus forward passes): shadow store = expert bank + 1,892 self-pool items + 40 planted W items. Three write-time scorers: (a) A-MAC-style factors (novelty = 1 - max cosine to store, task-type relevance, outcome confidence from the source episode's step count, redundancy with same-type items, specificity), combined by the published weighting where stated, else equal weights with a pre-registered threshold at the 60th percentile; (b) RPE-critic: surprise = reader NLL of the source trajectory's actions given the k=3 retrieved set at write time, utility = critic-predicted gain (a logistic model on surprise, novelty and type fitted on the first 500 stream games); (c) DIG-style confidence gain = change in reader log-probability of the successful action sequence of one held-out same-type train game with versus without the candidate in context (two forward passes). Sample 160 candidates stratified by each scorer's quartiles; measure ADD versus REPLACE-static on 24 games x 2 seeds each. Report Spearman(score, realized ADD) raw and disattenuated, and the realized ADD of admitted versus bypassed items per rule.
- E2 Stream passes (~6 h): pass A with per-item outcome Q (count-average) multiplying similarity in the retrieval rank; pass B with SF-AMS-style utility (usage, redundancy, recency) multiplying similarity. Log retrieved ids, positions, outcomes, and per-item feedback counts. Record the distribution of feedback events per store item and the retrieval share of the 40 planted W items per stream third.
- E3 Pruning audit (~5.8 h): for each of {random, outcome-Q bottom 20%, SF-AMS bottom 20%} and each feedback-count stratum {1-3, 4-7, >= 8}, sample 24 pruned items and measure realized LOO (REMOVE and REPLACE-static) on 16 games x 2 seeds. Metrics: harmless-prune rate (LOO <= 0), harmful-item capture (fraction of items with LOO <= -10 net that the rule prunes, using the E1 sample as the reference population), and the smallest stratum at which outcome-Q exceeds random by >= 0.15.
- E4 Composition check: the 40 planted W items and 40 highest-scoring admitted items are re-measured under a second composition (k=3 set with one self-written item swapped for an expert item) to test that admission-score rank agreement with realized value does not depend on the co-retrieved set (~3.2 h).
- Budget: E0 3.5 h + E1 6.4 h + E2 6 h + E3 5.8 h + E4 3.2 h = about 25 h on two A100s, one replica per GPU, E1 re-runs on one replica while E2 pass A runs on the other; nohup, pid files, resumable JSONL; pre-registration before E1.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Admission baselines: admit-all (shadow store), random admission at the same rate, similarity-to-existing-store threshold (novelty only), and the three write-time scorers.
- Pruning baselines: random pruning at matched count; outcome-Q; SF-AMS usage-decay; oracle pruning by realized LOO from E1 as the ceiling.
- Ablations: scorer components (novelty-only, redundancy-only, confidence-gain-only); DIG held-out game count 1 versus 3; feedback-count strata; outcome-Q with constant alpha versus count-average.
- Controls demanded by prior rounds: self-pool versus expert items reported separately; REPLACE-static placebo so admission value is net of the type procedure; token-matched planted items; both compositions in E4.
- Free baseline: nested-k logs give a position-level estimate for expert items to compare with the admission scorers on the same items.
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (headline) No write-time scorer exceeds Spearman 0.2 (disattenuated 0.3) with realized ADD value over the 160-candidate sample, and admitted minus bypassed realized ADD is within +/-5 net for every rule. Falsified if: any scorer reaches Spearman >= 0.4 with a bootstrap CI excluding 0.2, or admitted minus bypassed >= 5 net with CI excluding 0. Arm: E1 forced-retrieval cells on admitted versus bypassed strata. Not entailed: E0 confirms that realized values differ across items, so a scorer could in principle track them; confidence gain in particular could.
- P2 Feedback threshold: outcome-Q pruning exceeds random pruning in harmful-item capture by >= 0.15 only in the >= 8 feedback-event stratum and by < 0.10 in the 1-3 stratum. Falsified if: the >= 0.15 advantage appears already at 1-3 events (large-effect items are identifiable from a handful of outcomes). Arm: E3 outcome-Q versus random within the 1-3 stratum.
- P3 Coverage: fewer than 20% of store items reach >= 8 feedback events in the 3,553-game stream under similarity x utility retrieval. Falsified if: >= 35% do. Arm: E2 pass-A retrieval log.
- P4 Usage is not value: SF-AMS-style pruning's harmful-item capture is within +/-0.10 of random in every stratum, while its harmless-prune rate exceeds random (it removes redundant items with LOO near zero). Falsified if: SF-AMS capture >= random + 0.20 in any stratum. Arm: E3 SF-AMS cells.
- P5 Entrenchment versus correction: the planted W items' retrieval share in the last stream third relative to the first is <= 0.7 under outcome-Q and >= 1.5 under SF-AMS utility. Falsified (Q part) if: the ratio under outcome-Q is >= 0.9, i.e. verified failures do not demote wrong items because the co-retrieved helpful items rescue enough episodes. Falsified (SF-AMS part) if: the ratio is <= 1.1 because redundancy and recency terms cancel the usage loop. Arm: E2 pass A and pass B retrieval logs. The SF-AMS part is the weaker prediction since the usage loop is positive feedback by construction; it is reported as secondary and the Q part is the tested claim.
- Positive control that must pass first: E0 expert-versus-W separation >= 15 net; if it fails the audit is reported as underpowered, not as a null.
Measurement and Noise Control: All value measurements are paired on (game, seed) with the retrieved set changed at one slot. Per-item SE about 0.10 at 48 pairs; quartile strata of 40 items = 1,920 pairs give +/-4.5 net. Rank correlations use 1,000 item-level bootstraps and are disattenuated by split-seed reliability of realized value; both are reported. The E2 stream pass is repeated for pass A with a second stream seed to obtain the test-retest Spearman of per-item Q, which bounds how much of any pruning imprecision is estimator noise versus rule error. Harmful-item capture uses the E1 sample's realized values as the reference set, with the -10 net cutoff pre-registered. Cost is reported per decision: forward passes per candidate for each admission scorer, and episodes per item to reach split-half reliability 0.5 of realized value. Throughput logged per cell; both GPUs busy by overlapping E1 re-runs with E2 passes.

Name: memory_failure_blame_item_vs_set
Title: Who Is to Blame: Attributing Memory-Induced Failures of a Multi-Step Agent to a Single Retrieved Item or to the Set
Short Hypothesis: Among ALFWorld games that the agent solves without memory but fails with k=3 retrieval (memory-harmed games, defined on repeated seeds), most failures have a single culprit item whose removal alone restores success; culprits are enriched in cross-type items retrieved by object or receptacle similarity; a re-run-free proxy (share of the trajectory's actions up to the first deviation that are copied from an item) identifies the culprit better than position rank; and a culprit's harm largely survives re-embedding in a different background set, so blame is mostly an item property, with a measurable minority of set-caused failures where no single or pairwise removal restores success.
Related Work: The compliance trap (arxiv:2607.10608) diagnoses adoption of conflicting memory at the trajectory level and never attributes to an item or varies the co-retrieved set. MemAudit (arxiv:2605.23723, S2 listing) audits adversarially injected memory records by causal attribution and structural anomaly detection; it targets poisoning, not naturally accumulated benign items, and reports no item-vs-set split. Failure attribution for multi-agent systems assigns blame to agents and steps (Who&When arxiv:2505.00212; FALAT arxiv:2606.00765; A2P arxiv:2509.10401; TraceElephant arxiv:2604.22708; conformal error attribution arxiv:2605.06788), never to retrieved items. MINTEval (arxiv:2605.18565), Memora (arxiv:2604.20006) and MemoryAgentBench (arxiv:2507.05257) report interference failures at the question level only. Positional-bias work in RAG (arxiv:2505.15561, EMNLP 2025) finds distracting passages at top ranks in QA. Archived: retrieved_set_disagreement_gate (4.65) claimed harm lives in the set without item ground truth; wrong_action_fraction_dose (4.85) planted wrong items as a dose. Here the harmful items are natural and discovered by intervention, with a planted positive control only to calibrate the procedure.
Abstract: Benchmarks record that retrieved memory sometimes turns a solvable task into a failure, but no memory system or benchmark says which stored item did it, or whether any single item did. We attribute memory-induced failures in a multi-step agent by intervention. On ALFWorld with a Qwen3-32B reader, we first identify memory-harmed games from repeated k=0 and k=3 runs over the 274 validation games and a bank-disjoint train slice, then re-run each harmed game with each retrieved item removed, with each pair removed, and with a no-op repeat, on the same seeds. This yields a blame taxonomy (single-culprit, pair-culprit, diffuse, noise) with its seed-count reliability, a class analysis of culprits (cross-type vs same-type, expert vs self-written) against their retrieval share, a static-procedure arm that separates item-specific harm from type-level difficulty, and a re-embedding arm that asks whether a culprit still causes failure inside a different background set. We calibrate the procedure with a planted wrong-procedure item that must be recovered, and evaluate a cheap action-copy proxy and a DIG-style log-probability proxy against the intervention ground truth. The output is the first item-level blame ground truth for naturally accumulated agent memory, with its cost and noise stated.
Experiments: (1) Discovery: 274 validation games plus ~600 bank-disjoint train-stream games (partition verified before pre-registration) x 4 seeds x {k=0, k=3 natural sets from the retrieval policy}; the existing 2-seed logs count toward this; ~6,000 new episodes (~5 h). Harmed game: p0 >= 0.75 and p3 <= 0.25 over 4 seeds; helped game: the reverse; label stability checked by split-half seeds (1-2 vs 3-4). (2) Attribution cells on harmed games (expected 45-105): per (game, seed) S-i for i in slots 1-3, S-ij for the three pairs, and a no-op repeat: 7 episodes x 4 seeds x ~80 games = 2,240 (~1.9 h). Taxonomy: single-culprit if some p(S-i) >= p0 - 0.25; pair-culprit if no single but some p(S-ij) >= p0 - 0.25; diffuse otherwise; noise if the harmed label fails split-half. (3) Static-procedure arm (Measurement C prompt) on harmed games, 4 seeds, ~320 episodes: item-specific harm requires the static arm to succeed (p >= 0.75). (4) Positive control before any null: plant a token-matched wrong-procedure item into slot 2 of 100 helped games' sets, run S', S'-planted, S'-other, 4 seeds (1,200 episodes, ~1 h); the procedure must recover the planted item as culprit in >= 80% of cells that become harmed. (5) Re-embedding arm (second set composition): for single-culprit games, replace the two non-culprit items with the next two same-type items from the logs and re-run S'' and S''-culprit, 4 seeds (~50 games, 400 episodes). (6) Class analysis: culprit share by class (cross-type vs same-type; expert vs self-pool item in a self-pool replicate of steps 1-2 on the 274 validation games, ~2,200 + ~1,100 episodes) against the class's retrieval share from the logs; odds ratios with cluster bootstrap. (7) Proxies: action-copy score (fraction of actions up to the first deviation from any successful k=0 trajectory of the same game that appear, after object-id normalization, in item i and not in the others), DIG-style log-prob gain of the first deviating action with vs without item i (one forward pass per item), position rank and retrieval score; top-1 culprit accuracy on single-culprit cells. (8) Seed-count reliability: add 4 further seeds on harmed games for S and the three S-i cells (~1,300 episodes) to report split-half culprit agreement vs seed count and the re-run cost of a stable blame label. Total ~15,000 episodes, ~12.5 h on two A100s.
Baselines and Ablations: Position-rank blame (slot 1) and retrieval-score blame as re-run-free baselines; DIG-style log-prob proxy; static-procedure arm to net out type-level difficulty; self-pool replicate to compare expert vs self-written culprits; re-embedding arm to test whether blame transfers across backgrounds; no-op repeat and split-half seeds as the noise model; pairwise cells to distinguish pair-caused from diffuse; planted-culprit positive control to calibrate sensitivity.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 Single-culprit fraction among harmed games >= 0.6. Falsified if <= 0.4 (pair or diffuse majority), produced by the single- and pairwise-removal cells; not entailed because the compliance-trap account implies a single early-adopted item while distraction or reward-contamination accounts imply diffuse causes. P2 Culprit-class enrichment: odds ratio of cross-type items among culprits vs their share among all k=3 retrieved items >= 2.0. Falsified if OR <= 1.2, produced by the LOO cells and the retrieval logs; not entailed because same-type near-miss items (wrong receptacle or object) are an equally available culprit class. P3 Proxy: action-copy top-1 culprit accuracy >= 0.70 on single-culprit cells vs position-rank <= 0.45. Falsified if action-copy <= position-rank + 0.10, produced by the single-culprit cells. P4 Item-specific harm: the static-procedure arm succeeds (p >= 0.75) on >= 70% of single-culprit harmed games. Falsified if <= 40% (the type itself is the difficulty), produced by the static arm. P5 Transfer of blame: the culprit still produces failure (p(S'') <= 0.25 and p(S''-culprit) >= p0 - 0.25) in >= 60% of re-embedded single-culprit games. Falsified if <= 30% (harm is a set property), produced by the re-embedding cells. P6 Expert vs self-pool: self-pool sets have a harmed-game rate at least 1.5x the expert-bank rate and a higher diffuse share. Falsified if the rates are within +/-2 points and diffuse shares within 10 points, produced by the self-pool replicate. P7 Reliability: a culprit label needs >= 4 seeds to reach split-half agreement >= 0.8. Falsified if 2 seeds already give >= 0.8, produced by the added-seed cells.
Measurement and Noise Control: Harmed and restored labels are defined on 4-seed success rates, not single runs; the spurious-harm rate from seed noise is measured by split-half agreement of the harmed label, and only split-half-consistent games enter confirmatory cells. Culprit fractions and odds ratios carry cluster-bootstrap CIs over games; per-class cells are sized from the discovery phase and, if fewer than 40 harmed games appear in the validation set, the train slice is extended before pre-registration of thresholds. The no-op repeat gives the flip rate under no intervention as the null for restoration. The positive control must pass before P1-P5 are interpreted. Seed count for a stable blame label and the corresponding episode cost are reported as estimands. Claims are about the distribution of culprits over harmed games and item classes, not about individual items.
